id.description: ID of the generation to activate.

force.description: Force activates a generation that lags the head of the eventlog by more than the gate allows.

name.description: Name of the generation to activate.

handover_position.description: HandoverPosition is the eventlog position the outgoing generation had matched subscriptions up to. The incoming generation replays matching from there, so it is also the lower bound of the overlap the two generations may both have matched - and therefore of the window a subscription can see the same document version delivered twice.

chunk_id.description: ChunkID is the sequential chunk identifier.

events_url.description: EventsURL is a presigned GET URL for the chunk event zip.

first_event_at.description: FirstEventAt is the timestamp of the first event, RFC3339.

first_event_id.description: FirstEventID is the first eventlog ID in the chunk.

last_event_at.description: LastEventAt is the timestamp of the last event, RFC3339.

last_event_id.description: LastEventID is the last eventlog ID in the chunk.

manifest_hash.description: ManifestHash is the hex-encoded sha256 of the canonical manifest.

manifest_url.description: ManifestURL is a presigned GET URL for the signed chunk manifest.

content_url.description: ContentURL is a presigned GET URL for the canonical document JSON.

hash.description: Hash is the hex-encoded sha256 of the canonical document body, for a pre-download integrity check. The document object's own signature (the authoritative verification anchor) is delivered with the object.

version.description: Version is the latest archived version, or -1 if the document has been tombstoned (in which case there is no content URL).

attached_at_event_id.description: AttachedAtEventId is the log position the attachment was made at. Everything above it that the subscription matches is delivered to this destination, and the events between this position and the matcher noticing the attachment are replayed rather than lost.

elephant.distribution.BoolQuery.description: BoolQuery combines subqueries. Must and should contribute to the score, filter and must_not don't.

filter.description: Filter are subqueries that all have to match, without affecting the score of the hit.

minimum_should_match.description: MinimumShouldMatch is the number of should subqueries that have to match. Defaults to 1 when the query has no must or filter subqueries, 0 otherwise.

must.description: Must are subqueries that all have to match.

must_not.description: MustNot are subqueries that must not match.

should.description: Should are subqueries that may match, see minimum_should_match.

document_types.description: DocumentTypes to score against. Empty scores against every indexed type the caller can read. Use the types the subscription is going to name, the volume estimate is only about the documents it will see.

fields.description:
Fields to return with each top hit, named as flat index fields (e.g. "document.rel.section.uuid"), as in Search.Query. Only the top hits carry them - they are for reading the results, and the rest of the response is counts.
 The title is returned whether or not it is selected, so eyeballing the top hits needs nothing here; this is for the other things that say what a document is.

floor.description: Floor is the similarity below which documents are not scored at all, which bounds the work the call does. Documents below it are counted as non-matches at every rung of the ladder, so a floor above a candidate threshold would understate its volume and is an invalid argument. Absent uses a server-chosen floor.

language.description: Language to score against, as the language tag documents are indexed under. Empty scores against every language, matching a subscription that leaves the language out.

members.description:
Members to calibrate, scored the way a clause scores them: each document gets the highest similarity any of the members reaches. Pass the members of one clause to calibrate it as a whole, or a single member to calibrate it on its own. At least one is required.
 The min_similarity of a member is not used for scoring. When it is set it is added to the threshold ladder, so an existing threshold can be compared against the alternatives.

thresholds.description: Thresholds is an explicit ladder of candidate thresholds to estimate volume at. Empty lets the server pick a ladder from the observed distribution, which is the normal way to use this.

top_hits.description: TopHits is the number of highest-scoring documents to return for eyeballing. Defaults to 10, and is capped by the server.

window_days.description: WindowDays is the number of days back to score. Defaults to 7 and is capped by what the recent tier holds. A window shorter than a week will mistake the weekly publishing rhythm for a trend.

percentiles.description: Percentiles of the similarity distribution over the window, in ascending order of percentile.

scored_documents.description: ScoredDocuments is the number of documents in the window that scored at or above the floor. The percentiles are over these, not over every document in the window: the distribution of things that are at least vaguely related is what a threshold is chosen within.

thresholds.description: Thresholds is the ladder: what each candidate threshold would have matched over the window. This is the number a threshold is chosen on - a threshold is a volume decision, and matches per day is the volume it produces. Nothing here says anything about whether the matches are the right ones; that is what the top hits and PreviewSubscription are for.

top_hits.description: TopHits are the highest-scoring documents of the window, most similar first. Read them to find where the results stop being about what the clause is about; the similarity there is the threshold worth estimating volume at.

window_days.description: WindowDays is the window that was actually scored, which can be shorter than the requested one.

window_end.description: WindowEnd is the end of the scored window, RFC3339.

window_start.description: WindowStart is the beginning of the scored window, RFC3339.

elephant.distribution.CalibrationHit.description: CalibrationHit is one of the documents a calibration scored highest.

fields.description: Fields are the values the request's field selection asked for. The title is not among them unless the selection named it too.

first_published.description: FirstPublished is when the document was first published, RFC3339.

member_index.description: MemberIndex is the position in the calibrated members of the member that scored highest against this document.

similarity.description: Similarity the document scored, i.e. the highest similarity any of the calibrated members reached against any of its chunks.

title.description:
Title of the document, always returned. Choosing a threshold means reading down the top hits until they stop being about what the clause is about, and a list of UUIDs cannot be read that way.
 Empty for a document the index holds no title for, which is not the same as a document that isn't there.

uuid.description: UUID of the document. Pass it to Content.GetDocument to read it.

id.description: ID of the import job, or the upload ID of an un-finalized upload (they are the same identifier space).

elephant.distribution.ClauseProvenance.description: ClauseProvenance is the outcome of one vector clause.

clause_index.description: ClauseIndex is the position of the clause in SubscriptionSpec.vector_clauses.

members.description: Members of the clause with the similarity each of them scored. All members are reported, not only the ones that passed, so that a near miss is visible.

negate.description: Negate is whether the clause is negated, repeated here so that the provenance can be read without the subscription at hand.

activated_at.description: ActivatedAt is the time the generation was last activated, RFC3339, or empty if it has never been activated.

created_at.description: CreatedAt is the time of registration, RFC3339.

description.description: Description is an optional human-readable tag.

id.description: ID is assigned by the server on registration.

renditions.description: Renditions configured in the generation, one per asset kind.

elephant.distribution.ConfigGenerationSc.description: ConfigGenerationSchema references a schema version included in a generation. Spec is optional when the version is already stored; it is required when registering a new (name, version) pair.

elephant.distribution.ConfigGenerationTy.description: ConfigGenerationType configures a document type within a generation.

acknowledge_expiring_links.description: AcknowledgeExpiringLinks accepts that the destination's rendition links expire. They default to 24 hours, and a pushed object is durable: a customer mirroring the drop would hold, within a day, files whose asset links 404 - worse than an ordinary broken link, because it worked at delivery time and rots later. Set this, or set disable_rendition_signing, or configure the destination for variants that carry non-expiring public tokens.

files.description: Files that make up the import set, in load order.

upload_id.description: UploadId resumes an existing upload instead of creating a new one. The declared files must match the recorded declaration exactly; fresh presigned URLs are returned for all of them. Leave empty to create a new upload.

files.description: Files to upload, one per declared file, in declaration order.

upload_id.description: UploadId identifies the upload for resumption and finalization.

cluster.description: Cluster to build the generation on, named as the deployment declares it. Required. A deployment that only has the one cluster declares it as "default".

name.description: Name of the generation. A short readable codename is generated when it is left empty, which is what you want unless the name has to be predictable.

prefix.description: Prefix is the first segment of every index and alias name the generation owns, and defaults to the generation name. It has to be unique across generations - it is what keeps two generations from writing to each other's indexes - and a lowercase index name segment: it starts with a letter or a digit and continues with letters, digits, underscores or dashes.

keep_alive_seconds.description:
KeepAliveSeconds makes the subscription expiring: it is deactivated if nothing touches it for this long, and any authenticated RPC against it resets the clock. Clamped to at most seven days; a larger value is clamped, not rejected, and the value that was applied is on the returned subscription.
 Zero, the default, makes it durable: it lives until it is deleted. Expiry is independent of ownership — an organisation-owned subscription can be given a keep-alive, and a subject-owned one can be durable.

owner_tier.description:
OwnerTier selects who owns the subscription. "org", the default, makes it organisation-owned: it belongs to the organisation in the credentials of the caller, and any client of that organisation can manage and poll it. That is the tier for saved searches. "subject" makes it owned by the calling subject alone, which is the tier for subscriptions that follow one client session.
 The owner itself is never taken from the request: it is the org claim or the subject of the credentials the call was made with. This only picks which of the two it is.

elephant.distribution.CredentialStatus.description: CredentialStatus is what a destination will say about a stored credential: that it exists, and when it was written.

key_id.description: KeyID names the keyring entry it is encrypted under. Reported only to callers with "dist_admin", because it is the input to a key rotation and means nothing to an owner.

kind.description: Kind of credential. "s3" holds an access key id and secret; "sftp" holds a private key, a password, or both.

updated_at.description: UpdatedAt is when it was last written, RFC 3339.

name.description: Name of the generation to delete.
Name of the renderer whose secret to delete.

id.description: ID of the subscription to delete. Required. Deleting a subscription that doesn't exist is not an error.

elephant.distribution.DeliveryErasureObl.description: DeliveryErasureObligation is one destination that holds, or held, a pushed copy of an erased document.

cleared_at.description: ClearedAt is when the obligation was discharged, RFC3339, and empty while it is outstanding.

cleared_by.description: ClearedBy is always empty. It named the credentials the per-document operator write-off was recorded with, and that call was removed: every remaining reason is the system's own doing. The field is kept so its number is not re-used.

cleared_reason.description: ClearedReason is how it was discharged: "notified" (a deletion marker was delivered for every generation of the document this destination holds), "destination_deleted" (the destination and its credentials are gone, so there is nothing left to tell), or "already_terminated" (every generation this destination holds already had a deletion marker at the head of its chain, so nothing needed to be sent - the ordinary case for an erasure that follows a repository delete).

deliverable.description: Deliverable is whether a push worker will currently attempt this obligation. False means the destination is disabled, stalled, suspended, deleted or has no stored credential, and that the obligation will not clear until that is fixed. True is not a promise that it will clear: a destination whose stored credential no longer authenticates is deliverable and fails on every connect, which last_success_at is how you tell.

destination.description: Destination the copy was pushed to.

last_success_at.description: LastSuccessAt is when the destination last completed any delivery, RFC3339, and empty if it never has. Read beside deliverable: an attempting destination that has not succeeded since the erasure was ordered is failing rather than progressing.

objects_at_request.description: ObjectsAtRequest is how many objects the destination held when the erasure was ordered.

objects_outstanding.description: ObjectsOutstanding is how many objects of the erased content the destination is recorded as holding. It does NOT fall when the obligation clears: we delete nothing at a destination, so the count stands as the record of how much content the deletion marker is about. Above objects_at_request means a copy landed after the erasure was ordered, which is what re-opens a discharged obligation.

elephant.distribution.DeliveryField.description: DeliveryField is one entry in the vocabulary: the fold of every type's declaration of the name.

document_types.description: DocumentTypes are the types that declare the field, sorted. A document of any other type never carries it, so a condition naming this field is a no-match for those types.

kind.description: Kind is "keyword", "number", "text" or "geo". Every declaring type agrees on it - disagreement is refused when the generation is registered.

acknowledged.description: Acknowledgements the caller made, as name/true pairs.

actor.description: Actor is the subject of the credentials the call was made with.

applied_at.description: AppliedAt is when a deferred operation was carried out. Only a matcher skip is deferred; everything else applies in the call that records it and is stamped with the same timestamp.

from_position.description: FromPosition and ToPosition are the log or queue positions the operation moved between, zero where the kind has none.

subject_kind.description: SubjectKind is what the operation was about - "owner", "destination", "subscription" or "matcher" - and subject identifies it.

elephant.distribution.Destination.description: Destination is a destination as stored.

created_at.description: CreatedAt and UpdatedAt are RFC 3339 timestamps.

created_by.description: CreatedBy is the subject that created it.

credentials.description: Credentials reports which kinds of credential are stored, never their values.

deleted_at.description: DeletedAt is set on a deleted destination. Its inventory rows survive it as the record of what it was given.

last_success_at.description: LastSuccessAt is when it last delivered anything. The metrics answer this too and they die with the process, and "when did this last deliver" outlives a restart.

owner.description: Owner is the organisation or subject that owns the destination.

pending_deliveries.description: PendingDeliveries and OldestPendingAt describe the undelivered queue: how many rows and when the oldest was queued. Reported here so that a customer-facing UI does not have to scrape a metric.

stall_reason.description: StallReason is "queue_depth" or "queue_age" while stalled, and empty otherwise. The two are different conversations - a recipient that is down, and a recipient that is slow - and the state alone cannot say which.

stalled_at.description: StalledAt is when it stopped, RFC 3339, empty when it is running.

state.description: State is "ok" or "stalled". A stalled destination has stopped because its queue passed a limit, and only ResumeDestination restarts it.

suspended_at.description: SuspendedAt is set while the owner is suspended. Suspension is an administrative decision about the customer; a stall is evidence about the recipient, and clearing one does not clear the other.

elephant.distribution.DestinationSpec.description: DestinationSpec is a destination's definition. It is written whole by UpdateDestination: what is left out is cleared.

disable_rendition_signing.description: DisableRenditionSigning delivers rendition links unsigned. The same switch the Content API has, and the same warning: unsigned links are only useful where the asset is public.

disable_renditions.description: DisableRenditions delivers the stored canonical bytes with no rendition pass. It is the only form whose bytes can be checked against the document hash in the eventlog, and it takes precedence over the signing switch.

enabled.description:
Enabled is whether the destination delivers. A destination is created disabled unless this is set, because a destination with no credentials would otherwise start, fail and back off from the moment it exists.
 Enabled on its own is not enough to make a destination deliver: it also needs stored credentials. A destination with none never starts a worker and never issues a request, rather than falling back to whatever identity the service itself has.

format.description: Format of the delivered payload. "newsdoc" is the only format this build implements: it is what the Content API serves, through the same rendition and signing pass, so that moving a customer from pull to push does not change what they ingest.

include_html.description:
IncludeHTML delivers the document rendered to HTML with it: the envelope gains a rendered_html member beside document, an <article> fragment with the same rendition links the delivered document carries.
 It can be changed on an existing destination. It changes an envelope member, not an object key, so nothing a customer has already ingested is renamed or contradicted - the next delivery of a document simply carries the member, and the ingest contract's obligation to ignore unknown members is what a consumer that has not caught up relies on. The envelope version is not bumped for it.
 A retraction never carries HTML: it has no document to render. Neither does a document of a type the configuration renders no HTML for, and a render that had to fall back to the built-in renderers still ships.

max_queue_depth.description: MaxQueueDepth and MaxQueueAgeSeconds stop the destination's worker when its undelivered queue grows past them. They alert; they delete nothing, and what accumulated is still there when the destination is resumed. Zero means no limit, which is a decision rather than a default - a destination with no limit and a wedged recipient grows its queue until somebody notices.

name.description: Name of the destination, unique per owner. It is a handle for operators and for the customer, and it is not part of any object key.

name_template.description: NameTemplate decides what an object is called. "event" - "<prefix>/<event id>-<uuid>-<version>.json", zero-padded so lexical order is delivery order - is the default and suits a customer ingesting a stream of immutable objects. "document" - "<prefix>/<uuid>.json" - overwrites the earlier object on a correction, and suits a customer mirroring a drop. It is the shape every migrated newswire customer's ingest already keys on.

owner_tier.description: OwnerTier is "org" for a destination owned by the organisation of the caller, or "subject" for one owned by the calling subject. It defaults to "org", and it cannot be changed after creation: a subscription may only be attached to a destination with the same owner, so moving a destination between tiers would silently detach everything feeding it.

signing_audience.description: SigningAudience is the audience rendition links are signed for. It is derived from the owner for an organisation-owned destination and must be given for a subject-owned one, because a subject is a URI and an audience is a short name. A destination whose identity does not resolve is a configuration error, and this is where it is discovered.

sticky_window_seconds.description: StickyWindowSeconds is how long after a delivery decision this destination is owed follow-ups on a document it has been given: a correction to a story it received goes out even when the correction matches no rule. Zero means the deployment default, which is the retention period.

elephant.distribution.DocumentEvent.description:
DocumentEvent is one entry of the distribution eventlog, which is a transparency log: every entry is hashed over a canonical JSON payload, signed, and chained to its predecessor.
 The signed payload is exactly these nine fields, under these names: id, source, uuid (doc_uuid here), version, type, created_at, published_at, doc_hash and parent. Verifying an entry is: build that object, serialize it as RFC 8785 (JCS) canonical JSON, sha256 it, and check the digest and the ECDSA signature against the key the signature names, fetched from the unauthenticated JWKS at GET /signing-keys. Nothing else on this message is signed - event_type is derived from version, and first_published is a property of the document rather than of the event.
 The verification fields are only populated when the request asked for them; see GetNewDocumentsRequest.verification.

created_at.description: CreatedAt is when distribution emitted the event, in the canonical fixed-width RFC 3339 form used by the transparency log ("2006-01-02T15:04:05.000000Z", UTC, microsecond precision) — the same representation that the entry hash is computed over and that archived eventlog chunks carry. It is distribution's own clock, so an event for historical content carries a created_at long after the content was published. Use published_at to date the content.

doc_hash.description:
DocHash is the hex-encoded sha256 of the RFC 8785 canonical form of this version's document data, binding the event to the exact content it announced. Empty for a tombstone.
 Checking it takes two things. It covers the *version* named here, while load_documents delivers the document's current version, so a consumer verifying content fetches the exact version through Content.GetDocumentVersions or Content.GetDocument instead - the two agree only for an event that is still the document's latest. And it covers the stored bytes: rendition links are generated per response and signed for the caller's audience, so ask with disable_renditions or strip the generated rel="rendition" links before hashing.
 Verifying the log itself needs neither - the signature covers this field as a string, whatever content it names. Requires verification.

doc_uuid.description: DocUUID is the UUID of the affected document.

first_published.description:
FirstPublished is when the document first became public, in the same canonical fixed-width form. The event is about one version, and this is the per-document timestamp beside it: what a consumer groups and dates a document by, as opposed to the version. Equal to published_at for a document's first event, and unchanged by every event after it.
 Not part of the hashed event payload - it is a property of the document rather than of the event, read alongside it.

parent.description: Parent is the signature of event id-1, chaining the log, and is empty for event 1. A page therefore verifies as a chain on its own, and a consumer following the log checks that the first entry of a page names the signature of the last entry of the previous one. Requires verification.

published_at.description: PublishedAt is when the version was published in the source system: the time the "usable" status was created in the repository, or the publication time the record carried when the content was bulk imported. Same canonical fixed-width form as created_at, and part of the hashed event payload. This is the publication date of the content, and the timestamp the index anchors and ages documents on.

signature.description: Signature is the compact signature over the canonical payload, "v2.{key id}.{base64url sha256}.{base64url ECDSA signature}". The digest it carries must equal the one recomputed from the payload. Requires verification.

source.description: Source names the pipeline the event came from: the repository eventlog for content distributed as it is published, or a bulk import job for imported history. Part of the hashed payload.

type.description: Type of the document, e.g. "core/article", as the source event reported it - so a tombstone carries one too. Part of the hashed payload, empty string included: hash what is here, not what a document of that identity looks like now.

version.description: Version that was published (if this was a publish event).

deferred.description:
Deferred is set when load_documents or subset was requested and this item's document was not loaded because the response had reached its loading bound. Fetch it with Content.GetDocumentVersions.
 An item with neither a document nor deferred set has no document to load: it is a tombstone, or the document has been deleted or erased. Don't ask for it again.

rendered_html.description: RenderedHTML is the document rendered to HTML, when the request asked for it with include_html. An <article> fragment, and empty whenever there is no document to render it from: a deferred item, a tombstone, or a type the configuration renders no HTML for.

subset.description: Subset is the extracted subset of the document.

elephant.distribution.DocumentVersionRef.description: DocumentVersionRef identifies one version to load.

version.description: Version to load. Zero is the document's current version, as in GetDocument.

uuid.description: UUID of the document to erase.

elephant.distribution.ErasureStatus.description: ErasureStatus is the state of one document's erasure.

complete.description: Complete is true when the erasure is provably done, i.e. completed_at is set: nothing we control still holds the content, nothing more will be sent, and every destination that was given a copy has been sent a deletion marker. It does not mean the copies are gone from the destinations - push is append-only and we delete nothing there - and it has never covered content a customer has already ingested into their own systems.

completed_at.description: CompletedAt is when the erasure became provable, RFC3339, and empty while it is outstanding. It is set once no archived index snapshot holds a copy of the document any more and every destination that was given a copy has been told.

pending_deliveries.description: PendingDeliveries is every destination that was given a copy of this document, with how each one was accounted for. Entries are kept after they are discharged, because the record of who was given a copy and what happened to it is the compliance value: an outstanding entry is one with an empty cleared_at.

pending_partitions.description: PendingPartitions are the archived index partitions that still hold a copy. A mounted snapshot is read-only, so the copy in it only goes away when the partition is re-materialized, and the erasure is outstanding until every one of these has been.

requested_at.description: RequestedAt is when the erasure was ordered, RFC3339. A second request for the same document supersedes the first and resets this.

elephant.distribution.ExemplarDocuments.description: ExemplarDocuments is a set of documents used as an example of what to match, averaged into a single vector.

uuids.description: UUIDs of the exemplar documents, at least one. A document that isn't indexed, or is of a type indexed without embeddings, is an invalid argument.

annotation.description: Annotations can be used to differentiate between different extracted values.

role.description: Role can be used to differentiate between different extracted values.

value.description: Value is used for extracted attributes and data values.

extractor.description: Extractor index for the the extractor that produced the values.

elephant.distribution.FacetValues.description: FacetValues is the values a facet filter requires. A returned version has to carry all of them, and a request with several facets has to satisfy all of them - the filter is one containment test over the stored facet values. Narrowing to either of two sections is therefore two requests rather than one.

values.description: Values to match. These are document UUIDs, never labels: a section is a core/section document and the facet carries its UUID, so matching is exact and a human-readable name matches nothing at all.

elephant.distribution.FieldCondition.description: FieldCondition matches a keyword delivery field against a set of values. A field the document does not carry is a no-match, never an error: absence is a state the language has a meaning for.

field.description: Field is a delivery field name from GetDeliveryFields. It must be declared by the active configuration generation with kind "keyword", or the subscription is refused.

values.description: Values must be non-empty, for the same reason a group must be.

elephant.distribution.FieldMatch.description: FieldMatch is how a FieldCondition compares its values against the values the document carries. Declared at file level rather than nested in the condition because the OpenAPI renderer only registers file-level enums, and a nested one fails the specification generation outright.

expected_documents.description: ExpectedDocuments is the total number of documents in the import set, if the client knows it. Optional; when set it is recorded on the import and lets the load cross-check that it saw everything.

source.description: Source labels the imported events in the eventlog, so that consumers can tell the import apart from the live repository flow. Required, e.g. "ttdist". It cannot be a source the live sync worker writes.

upload_id.description: UploadId of the upload to finalize.

id.description: ID of the created import job, for GetImportStatus.

elephant.distribution.Fuzziness.description: Fuzziness is the edit distance allowed when matching terms.

edits.description: Edits is the maximum allowed Levenshtein edit distance. Valid values are 0, 1 and 2.

elephant.distribution.FuzzinessAuto.description:
FuzzinessAuto configures automatic fuzziness thresholds. The low and high values are the term length boundaries for the edit distance tiers:
 - Terms shorter than low characters must match exactly (0 edits). - Terms of low to high-1 characters allow at most 1 edit. - Terms of high characters or more allow at most 2 edits.
 Both zero uses the default thresholds, 3 and 6.

high.description: High is the term length where 2 edits start being allowed.

low.description: Low is the term length where 1 edit starts being allowed.

elephant.distribution.GeoCondition.description: GeoCondition matches a geo delivery field against a circle. The field is required: every condition names a registry field, and a document can carry coordinates in more than one place.

distance_km.description: DistanceKm is the radius in kilometres. The condition is satisfied when any of the field's points is within it, measured as a great-circle distance on a spherical earth.

field.description: Field must be declared with kind "geo".

latitude.description: Latitude of the circle's centre, in decimal degrees.

longitude.description: Longitude of the circle's centre, in decimal degrees.

known_id.description: KnownId is the generation ID the client already has; the call returns immediately when the active generation differs. Optional.

only_changed.description: OnlyChanged returns an empty response (with Unchanged=true) if the active generation matches KnownId.

wait_seconds.description: WaitSeconds is the maximum number of seconds to wait for the active generation to differ from KnownId. Defaults to 10. Optional.

unchanged.description: Unchanged is true if KnownId matched the active generation and OnlyChanged was set.

known.description: Known schema versions that the client already has. Optional.

only_changed.description: OnlyChanged only returns the schemas that have been changed.

wait_seconds.description: WaitSeconds is the maximum number of seconds to wait for changes, defaults to 10 seconds. Optional.

unchanged.description: Unchanged is set to true if no changes were done compared to known schema versions.

version.description: Version to get a URL for.

content_url.description: ContentURL is a presigned GET URL for the canonical document JSON.

hash.description: Hash is the hex-encoded sha256 of the canonical document body.

signature.description: Signature covers the document body, for end-to-end verification.

blind_before_event_id.description:
BlindBeforeEventId is the field-introduction boundary the caller acknowledged when the catch-up was scheduled, and BlindEvents how many events have so far been evaluated below it - against rows that predate a field the rules reference, where a condition on that field reads as a no-match rather than as a missing input.
 BlindEvents is the size of the shortfall that was accepted. It is the number the acknowledgement is worth nothing without.

catchup_from.description: CatchupFrom is where the running catch-up started, and CatchupPosition how far it has got. Both zero when none is running.

enrolled_at_event_id.description: EnrolledAtEventId is the position ordinary matching has covered the subscription from, and HeadEventId the current head of the log.

fields.description: Fields of the active generation, ordered by name.

generation.description: Generation is the configuration generation the vocabulary was read from. Every delivery_field row records the generation that produced it, so this is what a client compares against to tell whether what it is looking at is what produced the content it is looking at.

disable_rendition_signing.description: DisableRenditionSigning serves the document with generated but unsigned rendition URLs. See GetNewDocumentsRequest.disable_rendition_signing.

disable_renditions.description: DisableRenditions serves the document without any rendition links. See GetNewDocumentsRequest.disable_renditions.

include_html.description: IncludeHTML delivers the document rendered to HTML beside it. See GetNewDocumentsRequest.include_html.

renditions.description: Renditions selects the rendition variants to generate per asset kind. See GetNewDocumentsRequest.renditions.

uuid.description: UUID of the document to get.

version.description: Version to get, or 0 for the latest version.

first_published.description: FirstPublished is when the document first became public, in the same form. Immutable, and equal to published_at for a document that has only ever been published once. Empty for a document whose first-published record has been erased or was never written.

published_at.description: PublishedAt is when the returned version became public, in the canonical fixed-width RFC 3339 form ("2006-01-02T15:04:05.000000Z", UTC, microsecond precision). For a version served from the archive rather than the hot store this is empty: the archived object carries the document, not the timestamps of the row it was pruned from.

rendered_html.description: RenderedHTML is the document rendered to HTML, when the request asked for it with include_html. An <article> fragment; empty when the document's type renders no HTML.

types.description: Types that have been defined in the schema.

disable_rendition_signing.description: DisableRenditionSigning serves generated but unsigned rendition URLs.

disable_renditions.description: DisableRenditions serves documents without any rendition links.

include_html.description: IncludeHTML delivers each version rendered to HTML beside it. See GetNewDocumentsRequest.include_html.

load_documents.description: LoadDocuments is implied - this RPC exists to load documents - and is only here so that a caller asking for a subset can say it does not also want the whole document. It defaults to true when no subset applies.

renditions.description: Renditions selects the rendition variants to generate per asset kind.

subset.description: Subset returns extracted parts of each document instead of the document, keyed by the document types the expressions apply to.

versions.description: Versions to load. At least one, and the surplus beyond what one response will load comes back deferred.
Versions in the order they were requested.

uuid.description: UUID of the document to get the erasure status for.

document_type.description: DocumentType to get the mappings of. Required.

properties.description: Properties of the document type, sorted by name.

after.description: After returns new documents after the given event ID. A negative value is an offset from the newest event instead: -N returns the last N events (so at head 20, -5 yields events 16 through 20). The count is resolved against the log head at call time and capped at the same page size as a positive read. An offset reaching past the start of the log is clamped to the beginning.

disable_rendition_signing.description: DisableRenditionSigning serves documents with generated but unsigned rendition URLs instead of signing the rendition links for the caller's audience. Intended for internal consumers that store canonical content and re-sign for their own audience at their own delivery time; external consumers should leave it unset.

disable_renditions.description: DisableRenditions serves documents without any rendition links: the stored canonical bytes. This is the only mode whose payload matches the stored and archived document, so it is what a doc-hash verification against the transparency log must use. Takes precedence over disable_rendition_signing, which has no effect when this is set.

include_html.description:
IncludeHTML delivers the document rendered to HTML beside it, in rendered_html. It follows the document: an item whose document was not loaded - deferred, or not asked for - carries no HTML either, and a document of a type the active configuration does not render HTML for comes back without it rather than as an error.
 The HTML is an <article> fragment: block-level markup with no document frame, with the image links of the delivered document. Only data-block-id is a stable hook - see HTMLRenderingConfiguration.

load_documents.description: LoadDocuments should be set to true if you want the full documents in the response. If subset is used it will override load_documents.

renditions.description: Renditions selects the rendition variants to generate per asset kind (e.g. "image"). An absent kind - or an empty field within a present entry - falls back to the kind's configured defaults. An entry for a kind the active configuration doesn't declare is an invalid argument.

subset.description: Subset returns a subset of the documents as specified by a map of newsdoc value extractors keyed by the types that they should be applied to.

verification.description: Verification populates the transparency-log fields of every event: doc_hash, signature and parent. Together with the fields an event always carries they are the complete signed payload, so a consumer can recompute each entry's hash, verify the signature against the public keys at GET /signing-keys, and check that the page chains. Off by default: the three fields are a few hundred bytes an event that a consumer which doesn't verify would carry for nothing.

wait_ms.description: Wait is the maximum time in milliseconds to wait for new events when the read starts at the head of the log, mirroring the repository eventlog long poll. Defaults to 2000 and is capped at 8000. A negative value disables waiting so that at-head reads return an empty response immediately. Reads that can be answered immediately are always unaffected.

name.description: Name of the schema to get.

version.description: Version of the schema to get, optional. The currently active version of the schema will be returned if no version is specified.

keys.description: Keys is every published key, not just the one signing right now. A key stops being used for new signatures long before the entries it signed stop needing to be verifiable, so a verifier reading history needs the retired ones too, and picks the key a signature names rather than the newest.

id.description: ID of the subscription to get. Required.

caught_up.description: CaughtUp is true once the sync worker has replayed the repository eventlog up to the head it had when the replay started. It does not go back to false if the worker later falls behind: it reports that the walk through history is done, not the current lag. Compare Position against the repository eventlog head for that.

current.description: Current is the state the sync worker most recently reported, either "running" or "paused". Empty if the worker has never reported a state.

desired.description: Desired is the state the sync worker should be in, either "running" or "paused".

position.description: Position is the repository eventlog ID that the sync worker has processed up to.

elephant.distribution.HTMLRenderingConfi.description:
HTMLRenderingConfiguration configures delivery-time HTML rendering for the generation: which documents render, which image variant the rendered markup embeds, and the operator-registered renderers that extend or replace the built-in block renderers.
 HTML is rendered when a consumer asks for it - a pull request with include_html, or a push destination configured for it - never on the store path, and the result is cached per document version and configuration. The output is an <article> fragment: block-level HTML with no document frame, so a caller embeds it directly and a format that promises a whole document wraps it.
 Only data-block-id, which every top-level block element carries so that a consumer can correlate the markup back to the newsdoc blocks, is a versioned part of the markup. Element choices and class names may change between releases; do not write a consumer that depends on them. The top-level block is the addressable unit throughout: nested blocks carry no id, and a renderer that wants to change something inside one renders the block it sits in.

document_types.description: DocumentTypes are the document types that render HTML. Empty renders no type - a deployment opts its types in, so that planning documents and entity registries do not render markup nobody asked for. A request for HTML on a type outside the list yields no HTML and no error.

image_variant.description: ImageVariant is the rendition variant the rendered images link to. Empty defaults to "preview". It is service-level by design: the HTML is cached across callers, so the variant embedded in it cannot be a request parameter.

renderers.description:
Renderers extend the built-in block renderers, in declaration order. A renderer's triggers decide whether it is invoked for a document, not which blocks belong to it: every invoked renderer is called once with the whole document and may answer for any of its top-level blocks.
 Declaration order is what resolves a disagreement. Where two renderers return a replacement for the same block the one declared first wins and the other's entry is dropped; insertions are applied in the same order. A top-level block no renderer answered for is rendered by the built-ins.

deferred.description:
Deferred is set when load_documents or subset was requested and this hit's document was not loaded because the response had reached its loading bound - a hit whose document has aged out of the hot store is an archive read, and a page of them would make the query's response time a function of how old the results are. Fetch it with Content.GetDocumentVersions.
 A hit with neither a document nor deferred set has no document to load: it was deleted or erased since it was indexed.

fields.description: Fields are the values of the requested fields, keyed by field name. Fields without a value for the document are absent.

first_published.description: FirstPublished is when the document first became public, in the same form. Immutable, and what a backward-anchored type is partitioned and aged on.

id.description: ID is the UUID of the document. Pass it to Content.GetDocument to fetch the document itself, or ask the query for it with load_documents.

published_at.description:
PublishedAt is when the indexed version of the document became public, in the canonical fixed-width RFC 3339 form ("2006-01-02T15:04:05.000000Z", UTC, microsecond precision).
 It dates the projection that matched, which is not necessarily the document that was loaded: a document corrected since it was indexed is delivered as it stands now, and this is the version the hit was matched on. Empty for a hit out of an index that predates the field.

rendered_html.description: RenderedHTML is the loaded document rendered to HTML, when the query asked for it with include_html. It is rendered from the version that was loaded - the current stored version - not from the projection the hit was matched on.

score.description:
Score is the relevance score of the hit. Only meaningful for hits ordered by relevance; a sorted query leaves it at zero.
 For a knn query the score is the cosine similarity of the document to the query vector, in [-1, 1] and on the same scale as KnnQuery.min_similarity: the server converts it out of OpenSearch's score space so that the two can be compared directly. For a text query it is an unbounded BM25 score, comparable between hits of the same query and meaningless between queries.

subset.description: Subset is what the document type's extractors collected from the delivered document, when the query named the type in subset.

version.description: Version is the stored version the loaded document or subset was taken from, and zero when neither was requested or the document was no longer there to load.

elephant.distribution.HitsTotal.description: HitsTotal is the number of matching documents. The count is exact up to a server-side limit, above which it is reported as a lower bound.

relation.description: Relation is "eq" when value is the exact number of matches, and "gte" when the matches were only counted up to value.

value.description: Value is the number of matching documents, interpreted according to relation.

elephant.distribution.ImportFile.description: ImportFile declares one file of an import upload.

name.description: Name of the file within the upload, e.g. "documents-2024-Q2.ndjson.gz". Names must be unique within the upload. Files are loaded in declaration order.

sha256.description: Sha256 is the hex-encoded sha256 of the file contents, verified at finalization.

size.description: Size of the file in bytes.

elephant.distribution.ImportFileUpload.description: ImportFileUpload is the upload destination for one declared file.

expires_at.description: ExpiresAt is when the URL stops working, RFC3339. Resume the upload to get fresh URLs.

name.description: Name of the file, as declared.

upload_url.description: UploadUrl is a presigned PUT URL for the file contents. Object keys and the presigning mechanism are internal - the URL is used as-is and never parsed.

elephant.distribution.ImportStatus.description: ImportStatus is the recorded state of one import job.

created_at.description: CreatedAt is when the import was finalized, RFC3339.

current_file.description: CurrentFile is the declared file the load is working through, and the last one once the import is done.

documents_loaded.description: DocumentsLoaded is how many documents have been stored so far.

error.description: Error is what a failed import failed with, empty otherwise.

expected_documents.description: ExpectedDocuments is the total declared at finalization, or zero if none was.

quarter_high_water_mark.description: QuarterHighWaterMark is the most recent quarter the import has fully loaded, e.g. "2024q2", empty until the first quarter completes. Quarters are loaded in order, so overlay-pressure re-materializations of quarters the mark has not passed are held until it does - one rebuild per touched quarter, after the import has moved on. Deadline-driven re-materializations (tombstone, erasure) are never held.

source.description: Source the imported events carry in the eventlog.

status.description: Status is "pending" until the load starts, "loading" while it runs, and "done", "failed" or "cancelled" when it ends. A failed import is resumed by the service, not re-created: documents are idempotent per version, so the load continues from its recorded progress. Only CancelImport moves a job to "cancelled", and only from there does the loader move on to the jobs queued behind it.

updated_at.description: UpdatedAt is when the recorded state last changed, RFC3339.

elephant.distribution.IndexGeneration.description: IndexGeneration is one complete set of search indexes: everything under one index name prefix, on one cluster, with an eventlog cursor of its own.

activated_at.description: ActivatedAt is when it was last activated, RFC3339, and empty for a generation that has never served.

active.description: Active is whether this is the generation that search, calibration and subscription matching use.

cluster.description: Cluster the generation's indexes live on, named as the deployment declares it. Clusters are configuration, so their URLs and credentials are never part of a response.

created_at.description: CreatedAt is when the generation was registered, RFC3339.

enabled.description: Enabled is whether an indexer is run for the generation. A disabled generation keeps its indexes but stops consuming the eventlog, and falls behind for as long as it stays that way.

name.description: Name of the generation. It identifies the generation in these RPCs, in the generation override on Search.Query, and in metric labels.

prefix.description: Prefix is the first segment of every index and alias name the generation owns, and what scopes it: no two generations share one.

elephant.distribution.IndexGenerationSta.description: IndexGenerationStatus is a generation together with how far it has got.

lag.description: Lag is how far the generation is behind the head of the eventlog, which is what the activation gate is checked against.

position.description: Position is the eventlog ID the generation's indexer has processed up to, and zero for a generation whose indexer has not stored a position yet - either because it has not started or because it is still draining the archive.

elephant.distribution.KnnQuery.description:
KnnQuery is a semantic query: it looks up the documents whose embeddings are closest to a query vector, rather than the documents that contain the query terms.
 The clause has two independent choices, and the server validates both - the fields are plain fields rather than oneofs so that the combinations can be relaxed later without renumbering, but an invalid combination is rejected as an invalid argument, it is never guessed at.
 1. Where the query vector comes from: exactly one of text and vector. 2. How many neighbours come back: exactly one of k and min_similarity.
 Similarity is cosine similarity throughout, in the range [-1, 1], where higher means closer and 1 means identical direction. The embeddings are normalized, so this is the same dial as maximum inner product; the server converts from OpenSearch's own score space so that both min_similarity and the per-hit scores are stated as cosine similarity. Hit.score for a knn hit is therefore directly comparable to min_similarity, which is how a threshold is found: run a k query, look at where the results stop being relevant, and read the threshold off the scores.
 Thresholds are model-dependent and are not portable between deployments or across an embedding model upgrade. Treat a min_similarity value as something to recalibrate, not as a constant.

k.description: K is the number of nearest neighbours to retrieve. The hits come back ordered by similarity, and there are always k of them (fewer only when the filtered candidate set is smaller), no matter how poor the last ones are - a k query has no relevance floor. Mutually exclusive with min_similarity, and one of the two must be set.

min_similarity.description:
MinSimilarity turns the clause into a radial query: every document at or above this cosine similarity is a hit, however many that turns out to be, up to size. Use it when "everything that is at least this close" is the question - it makes a result set that does not silently pad itself with weak matches the way a fixed k does, and it is the same predicate that subscriptions match on, so a query is how a subscription threshold is previewed.
 Cosine similarity in [-1, 1]; higher is closer. Mutually exclusive with k, and one of the two must be set. The field is optional so that a floor of 0 - every document that isn't pointing away from the query - can be asked for, and is distinct from not asking for a radial query at all.

text.description: Text to search for, embedded server-side with the current embedding model. This is the normal way to run a semantic query, and the only one that survives a model upgrade unchanged, since the server re-embeds the text with whatever model is current.

vector.description: Vector to search for, as a raw embedding. Advanced use: the caller has to produce it with the same model and dimension as the index, and a model upgrade invalidates it. Prefer text unless the vector comes from somewhere the server cannot re-derive it from. A vector of the wrong dimension is an invalid argument.

expression.description: Expression is a newsdoc value extraction expression.

template.description: Template is the template that turns the extracted values into a label.

after_chunk_id.description: AfterChunkID lists chunks after the given chunk ID; 0 to start.

chunks.description: Chunks in this page, in ascending chunk-ID order.

cursor.description: Cursor from a previous response; empty to start a new drain.

next_cursor.description: NextCursor is empty when the catalog has been exhausted.

watermark_event_id.description: WatermarkEventID is the last archived event ID as of the start of the drain. A consumer that has drained the catalog should tail Content.GetNewDocuments from this ID: everything up to it is covered by the catalog, everything after it by the tail.

before.description: Before is the highest generation ID to return; defaults to the latest. Use the smallest returned ID to paginate further into the past.

generations.description: Generations without schemas or type configurations populated.

subject_kind.description: SubjectKind and subject filter to one destination, owner or subscription. Empty lists everything.

owner_tier.description: OwnerTier filters on ownership: "org" for the destinations of the organisation, "subject" for the caller's own. Empty lists both.

eventlog_head.description: EventlogHead is the ID of the last event in the distribution eventlog, the position a generation that has caught up converges on.

after.description:
After is a cursor from a previous response. Empty starts at the earliest end of the interval.
 Unlike the published day, this cursor sits on a mutable key: a rescheduled item moves, so it can cross a page boundary while a client pages an interval, and appear twice or not at all. Bounded and deliberate for a calendar - do not read exactness into it.

disable_rendition_signing.description: DisableRenditionSigning serves documents with generated but unsigned rendition URLs.

disable_renditions.description: DisableRenditions serves documents without any rendition links.

document_types.description: DocumentTypes to include. At least one.

facets.description: Facets narrows the result to documents carrying the given values. See ListPublishedVersionsRequest.facets.

from.description: From is the start of the interval on the planned date, inclusive, as an RFC 3339 timestamp with an offset. Required. See ListPublishedVersionsRequest.from for why this is an interval and not a day.

include_html.description: IncludeHTML delivers each entry's document rendered to HTML beside it. See GetNewDocumentsRequest.include_html.

limit.description: Limit is the maximum number of entries to return. Defaults to 50 and is capped at 200.

load_documents.description: LoadDocuments delivers the document with each entry.

renditions.description: Renditions selects the rendition variants to generate per asset kind.

subset.description: Subset returns a subset of each document. Overrides load_documents for the types it names.

to.description: To is the end of the interval, exclusive, as an RFC 3339 timestamp with an offset. Required.

inline_horizon.description: InlineHorizon is the oldest instant whose documents still come back with the response. See ListPublishedVersionsResponse.inline_horizon.

items.description: Items are what is planned for the interval, earliest first. Current versions only, so superseded_at is always empty.

next.description: Next is the cursor to pass as after for the next page, and empty at the end of the interval.

after.description: After is a cursor from a previous response. Empty starts at the newest end of the interval. Cursors are opaque and stay valid indefinitely: the sort key of an entry is its publication time, which never changes.

disable_rendition_signing.description: DisableRenditionSigning serves documents with generated but unsigned rendition URLs. See GetNewDocumentsRequest.disable_rendition_signing.

disable_renditions.description: DisableRenditions serves documents without any rendition links. See GetNewDocumentsRequest.disable_renditions.

document_types.description: DocumentTypes to include. At least one; several at a time is the normal shape, as a newsroom flow lists flashes, articles and editorial information together.

facets.description: Facets narrows the result to versions carrying the given values, keyed by facet name. A version has to carry every named facet and every value within it. The extraction is per type and per version, so a version that carried a section when it was published matches even if a later version doesn't - which is right for a publication log: it was published in that section at that minute.

from.description:
From is the start of the interval, inclusive, as an RFC 3339 timestamp with an offset. Required.
 The server has no notion of a day: what a day is, in which timezone, and whether the boundary falls at midnight or at the start of a shift is the client's decision. The interval is normalised to UTC for the scan, so an offset is how a local day is expressed.

include_html.description: IncludeHTML delivers each entry's document rendered to HTML beside it. See GetNewDocumentsRequest.include_html.

limit.description: Limit is the maximum number of entries to return. Defaults to 50 and is capped at 200.

load_documents.description: LoadDocuments delivers the document with each entry. Unlike Search.Query, which loads the current version, this loads the version the entry is.

renditions.description: Renditions selects the rendition variants to generate per asset kind. See GetNewDocumentsRequest.renditions.

subset.description: Subset returns a subset of each document as specified by a map of newsdoc value extractors keyed by the types they apply to. Overrides load_documents for the types it names.

to.description: To is the end of the interval, exclusive, as an RFC 3339 timestamp with an offset. Required. The span is capped by the server; a wider interval is an invalid argument.

inline_horizon.description:
InlineHorizon is the oldest instant whose documents still come back with the response, in the canonical fixed-width RFC 3339 form.
 It is not a limit on what the view can answer. Retention drops document bodies and keeps their bookkeeping, so any interval can be listed; what changes past this point is that every document has to be streamed in with GetDocumentVersions rather than delivered inline. A client uses it to decide how hard to prefetch.

items.description: Items are the publication events of the interval, newest first.

next.description: Next is the cursor to pass as after for the next page, and empty at the end of the interval.

include_deactivated.description: IncludeDeactivated includes subscriptions that have expired and are waiting to be reaped. They are left out by default.

owner_tier.description: OwnerTier filters on ownership: "org" for the subscriptions of the organisation of the caller, "subject" for those owned by the calling subject. Empty lists both.

subscriptions.description: Subscriptions the caller can see, most recently created first.

deferred.description: Deferred is set when this version was beyond the response's loading bound. Ask again - a client that re-requests what it did not get makes progress.

first_published.description: FirstPublished is when the document first became public, same form.

found.description: Found is false when the version is in neither the store nor the archive: erased, deleted, or never distributed. Don't ask again.

published_at.description: PublishedAt is when this version became public, in the canonical fixed-width RFC 3339 form. Empty for a version served from the archive.

rendered_html.description: RenderedHTML is this version rendered to HTML, when the request asked for it with include_html. Absent for a deferred version, exactly as the document is.

subset.description: Subset is what the type's extractors collected from it.

version.description: Version that was loaded. For a request that asked for version zero this is the version the document is currently at.

elephant.distribution.MappingField.description: MappingField is an alternative indexing of a property.

name.description: Name of the field, appended to the property name with a dot to query it.

type.description: Type of the field, from the same vocabulary as the property type, plus "prefix" for fields analysed for prefix matching.

elephant.distribution.MappingProperty.description: MappingProperty is a searchable field of a document type.

fields.description: Fields are alternative indexings of the property, queried as "name.field". A text property commonly has a "keyword" field for exact matching and sorting, and a "prefix" field for as-you-type matching.

name.description: Name of the property, as used in queries.

path.description: Path is the property that an alias property points to. Empty for everything but aliases.

type.description: Type of the property: "text", "keyword", "date", "long", "double", "boolean", or "alias" for a property that is another name for the property named by path.

elephant.distribution.MatchAllQuery.description: MatchAllQuery matches every document. Useful as the base of a query that only filters, and for browsing a type by sort order.

elephant.distribution.MatchGroup.description: MatchGroup combines rules. Negation lives here and nowhere else: a negated leaf is a negated group of one, which is more typing in the editor and one fewer place for the meaning of "not" to differ.

negate.description: Negate inverts the group's result, after the requirement is applied.

rules.description: Rules must be non-empty. An empty group is rejected at write time rather than given a meaning: ALL of nothing is true, ANY of nothing is false, and negation flips both, so every reading is defensible and three of the four are a customer surprise.

elephant.distribution.MatchPhraseQuery.description: MatchPhraseQuery matches analysed text where the terms occur in the given order, next to each other.

value.description: Value to match as a phrase.

elephant.distribution.MatchProvenance.description: MatchProvenance records what fired, so that a match can be explained and so that feedback about it can be routed to the part of the subscription that caused it.

clauses.description: Clauses are the vector clauses of the subscription, in the order they are stored in, with the similarities they scored.

query_matched.description: QueryMatched is whether the query part of the subscription matched. False when the subscription has no query part.

rule_ids.description: RuleIDs are the Rule.id values of the conditions that admitted the document, on a delivery-class match. Empty on a notification match, where query_matched and clauses are the provenance.

elephant.distribution.MatchQuery.description: MatchQuery matches analysed text: the value is run through the analyser of the field, and a document matches if any of the resulting terms do.

boost.description: Boost multiplies the score contribution of the clause. Defaults to 1.

elephant.distribution.MatchRequirement.description: MatchRequirement is how a MatchGroup combines the rules it holds. Declared at file level rather than nested in the group because the OpenAPI renderer only registers file-level enums, and a nested one fails the specification generation outright.

elephant.distribution.MemberProvenance.description: MemberProvenance is the similarity one clause member scored against the document.

member_index.description: MemberIndex is the position of the member in VectorClause.members.

passed.description: Passed is whether the similarity reached the threshold of the member. In a negated clause a passing member is what would have excluded the document, so all of them are false on a match.

similarity.description: Similarity is the highest cosine similarity between the vector of the member and the chunk embeddings of the document, on the same scale as VectorClauseMember.min_similarity.

elephant.distribution.MultiMatchQuery.description: MultiMatchQuery matches analysed text against several fields at once.

boolean_and.description: BooleanAnd requires all terms of the query to match.

boost.description: Boost multiplies the score contribution of the clause. Defaults to 1.

fields.description: Fields to match against. A field can carry a boost as a "^"-suffix, e.g. "document.title^3".

minimum_should_match.description: MinimumShouldMatch is the number of query terms that must match when the terms are combined with "or". Takes the full minimum-should-match expression syntax, e.g. "2" or "75%".

prefix_length.description: PrefixLength is the number of leading characters that fuzzy matching leaves unchanged. Defaults to 0.

tie_breaker.description: TieBreaker is how much the score of matches in other fields than the best-scoring one contributes, between 0 and 1. Defaults to 0, i.e. only the best field counts.

type.description: Type is the multi-match query type. Valid values are best_fields, most_fields, cross_fields, phrase, phrase_prefix and bool_prefix. Defaults to best_fields.

after_event_id.description: AfterEventID returns matches with a higher event ID than this one. Start at 0 to read the log from the beginning, and pass the event ID of the last match you processed on every call after that.

subscription_id.description: SubscriptionID to read matches for. Required.

wait_ms.description:
WaitMS is the maximum time in milliseconds to wait for a match when there is nothing to return yet. Defaults to 2000 and is capped by the server. A negative value disables waiting, so a caller that is draining a backlog returns immediately at the end of it. A call that can be answered from the log doesn't wait.
 Waiting is not a guarantee of getting the whole batch: the server waits for the first match, gives the rest of the batch a moment to land, and returns what is there. Keep polling.

matches.description: Matches in ascending event ID order. Empty when the wait ran out without anything matching, which is the normal idle response.

elephant.distribution.PrefixQuery.description: PrefixQuery matches values that start with the given value. Run it against a keyword field, or against a field that the mappings report as "prefix": those are analysed for prefix matching and are much cheaper to search as you type.

boost.description: Boost multiplies the score contribution of the clause. Defaults to 1.

value.description: Value that the field must start with.

elephant.distribution.PreviewMatch.description: PreviewMatch is a document that a previewed subscription would have matched. It is the match log entry as it would have looked, minus the event: a preview runs against the indexed documents of the window, not against the events that produced them.

fields.description: Fields are the values the request's field selection asked for. The title is not among them unless the selection named it too.

first_published.description: FirstPublished is when the document was first published, RFC3339. This is what max_age_seconds is evaluated against.

title.description:
Title of the document, always returned. A dry run is read to decide whether the matches are the right ones, and that judgement is made on what the documents are, not on their identifiers.
 Empty for a document the index holds no title for.

uuid.description: UUID of the document. Pass it to Content.GetDocument to read it.

fields.description: Fields to return with each match, named as flat index fields (e.g. "document.rel.section.uuid"), as in Search.Query. The title is returned whether or not it is selected.

size.description: Size is the maximum number of matches to return, most recent first. Defaults to 50 and is capped by the server. The total is reported separately, so a preview that returns the first page still says how much the subscription would have fired.

window_days.description: WindowDays is the number of days back to evaluate. Defaults to 7 and is capped by what the recent tier holds.

matches.description: Matches in the window, most recently published first.

matches_per_day.description: MatchesPerDay is total spread over the window, the rate the subscription would have fired at. A subscription that fires more often than the surface it feeds can carry needs a tighter threshold, not a filter on the consuming side.

window_end.description: WindowEnd is the end of the evaluated window, RFC3339.

window_start.description: WindowStart is the beginning of the evaluated window, RFC3339.

elephant.distribution.PublishedVersion.description: PublishedVersion is one stored document version in a daily view.

anchor.description: Anchor is the date the document is planned for, in the same form: the resolved partition anchor of a forward-anchored type. Empty for types that carry no dates of their own. This is what ListPlannedVersions orders and filters on.

deferred.description:
Deferred is set when load_documents or subset was requested and this entry's document was not loaded because the response had reached its loading bound. Fetch it with Content.GetDocumentVersions, passing doc_uuid and version.
 An entry with neither a document nor deferred set has no document to load - it has been erased - so don't ask for it again.

doc_uuid.description: DocUUID is the UUID of the document.

first_published.description: FirstPublished is when the document first became public, in the same form. Equal to published_at for a version that is the document's first.

published_at.description: PublishedAt is when this version became public, in the canonical fixed-width RFC 3339 form ("2006-01-02T15:04:05.000000Z", UTC, microsecond precision). This is what ListPublishedVersions orders and filters on.

rendered_html.description: RenderedHTML is this version rendered to HTML, when the request asked for it with include_html. It follows the document: a deferred entry carries no HTML either.

subset.description: Subset is what the document type's extractors collected from the delivered document, when the request named the type in subset.

superseded_at.description:
SupersededAt is when a later version of the document was published, in the same form, and empty while this is the current version. A published-day view renders superseded entries as history: they are what was published at that minute, not what stands now.
 Always empty in ListPlannedVersions, which only returns current versions.

version.description: Version of the document this entry is, in the same numbering as DocumentEvent.version and Content.GetDocument.

elephant.distribution.Query.description: Query is a single query clause. Exactly one of the conditions must be set; an empty Query is an invalid argument.

exists.description: Exists matches documents that have a value for the named field.

query_string.description: QueryString is a query in the query string mini-language. Use it for user-entered search expressions; prefer the structured clauses for queries the client builds itself.

date_from.description:
DateFrom and DateTo restrict the result to documents whose anchor falls in the interval, as RFC 3339 timestamps. The interval is half-open - from is inclusive, to is exclusive - so consecutive windows tile without returning a document on the boundary twice. Either bound may be left empty for an interval open on that side.
 The anchor is whatever the document type is partitioned on, not a named field: first_published for a type dated by publication, and the time expression the document was routed on for one dated by what it describes - a planning item covering next week is in next week's window, whenever it was written. So the same request means "in this period" for every type, and a caller does not have to know which field a type is anchored on. Types that aren't partitioned by time, the entity registries such as sections and authors, have no anchor and are returned regardless, exactly as the tier window leaves them alone.
 This is the way to scope a semantic query to a period, and the only way: a range clause cannot be combined with knn - see query - so a date range written that way is an invalid argument rather than an answer that cannot be trusted. The interval is applied around the k-NN clause rather than inside it, so it also narrows the query to the partitions the interval intersects, and the neighbours are drawn from those partitions rather than from the whole tier. Within them the interval is applied to the neighbours after they are picked, so a k-bounded query whose interval covers part of a partition can return fewer than k hits; a radial query bounded by min_similarity is unaffected, which is what to reach for when the count matters.

disable_rendition_signing.description: DisableRenditionSigning serves the documents with generated but unsigned rendition URLs. See GetNewDocumentsRequest.disable_rendition_signing.

disable_renditions.description: DisableRenditions serves the documents without any rendition links. See GetNewDocumentsRequest.disable_renditions.

document_types.description:
DocumentTypes to search. Empty searches all types the caller can read. A type that isn't indexed is an invalid argument.
 For a semantic query (knn) the empty list is every indexed type that carries embeddings: the types that don't are skipped rather than refused, since a deployment normally indexes entity registries that have no vectors beside the temporal types that do. A type that is named explicitly is still an invalid argument when it has no embeddings - it is a question that cannot be answered, and an empty result would look like one.

fields.description: Fields to return with each hit, named as flat index fields (e.g. "document.title"). Empty returns hits without field values, which is the cheapest form when the caller only needs the UUIDs.

from.description: From is the number of hits to skip, for paging through a result set. Deep paging is bounded by the server; use a narrower query or a sort on a stable field instead of paging far into a large result.

generation.description:
Generation answers the query from a named index generation instead of the active one, naming it as Configuration.ListIndexGenerations does. Empty is the active generation, and the only value an ordinary caller may send: naming a generation requires the "dist_admin" scope.
 It is the validation surface for a rebuild or a move to another cluster. A candidate generation is built and kept up to date while the active one serves, and this is how real queries are pointed at it and the results compared before it is activated. A generation that doesn't exist, or one whose cluster is unreachable, is an error rather than a silent fall back to the active generation - a comparison that quietly queried the wrong index set would be worse than no comparison.

include_html.description:
IncludeHTML returns each hit's document rendered to HTML beside it, in rendered_html. It follows the loaded document, so it needs load_documents or subset, and it requires the same "dist_read" scope they do. A hit whose document was deferred or is no longer stored comes back without HTML, as it comes back without a document.
 The HTML is an <article> fragment rendered from the same delivered document, with the same rendition links. See Configuration's HTMLRenderingConfiguration for what the markup promises.

language.description: Language to search, as the language tag the documents are indexed under, e.g. "sv" or "sv-se". Required: a query targets exactly one language series so that fan-out stays explicit. An unknown language is an invalid argument.

load_documents.description:
LoadDocuments returns the document itself with each hit, as Content.GetDocument would serve it: the current stored version, with the rendition links generated and signed for the caller. It requires the "dist_read" scope on top of the search scope - "dist_search" alone grants queries over the index, not the content behind it.
 A page of hits is what bounds it - the server's page size cap applies to a query that loads documents as it does to any other. A hit whose document is no longer stored is returned without one rather than failing the query.

renditions.description: Renditions selects the rendition variants to generate per asset kind. See GetNewDocumentsRequest.renditions.

size.description: Size is the maximum number of hits to return. Defaults to 50, and is capped by the server.

sort.description: Sort order of the hits. Empty sorts by relevance, descending.

subset.description:
Subset returns extracted parts of the documents instead of the whole of them, as a map of newsdoc value extractors keyed by the document types they apply to. It overrides load_documents for the types it names, and requires the same "dist_read" scope.
 Extraction runs on the delivered document, so an extracted image block carries the same generated rendition links the whole document would have been served with.

tier.description:
