Tier to search: "recent" for the rolling recent window, "all" for the recent window plus the archive. Empty defaults to "recent". Any other value is an invalid argument.
 "recent" is not "whatever the cluster happens to hold locally". It applies an implicit window on the document's anchor timestamp, so that recent means the same thing on the first day of a quarter as on the last. For document types anchored on when they happened - news, and everything else dated by publication - that window is a first_published no older than the configured recent window, 30 days by default. Types that aren't partitioned by time, the entity registries such as sections and authors, are never windowed and are returned in full by both tiers.
 "all" searches the archive set as well. The archive is served from snapshots mounted on separate nodes, so it answers more slowly, and the higher latency is accepted rather than worked around - which is why it is an explicit choice and not the default. Scope an archive query with a range on the anchor field whenever you can: given a range, the server resolves the query to the archived partitions that intersect it instead of fanning out over every quarter ever indexed.
 A document that has been corrected after its partition was archived exists in both tiers. Hits are collapsed on the document UUID, and the field values reported are those of the highest indexed version, so a cross-tier query never returns the same document twice and never reports the superseded copy's values.

hits.description: Hits in the requested order, at most size of them.

elephant.distribution.RangeCondition.description: RangeCondition matches a number delivery field against a closed interval. Both bounds are optional and both are inclusive; a condition with neither bound matches any document that carries the field at all.

field.description: Field must be declared with kind "number".

from.description: From is the inclusive lower bound. Unset means unbounded below - which is why it is optional rather than defaulted: a zero lower bound and no lower bound are different filters, and on a newsvalue they are very different filters.

to.description: To is the inclusive upper bound. Unset means unbounded above.

elephant.distribution.RangeQuery.description: RangeQuery matches a field against an interval. The bounds are written as strings and parsed according to the type of the field, so a date field takes RFC 3339 timestamps and a numeric field takes numbers. At least one bound must be set; combining a lower and an upper bound gives a closed interval.

gt.description: Gt is an exclusive lower bound.

gte.description: Gte is an inclusive lower bound.

lt.description: Lt is an exclusive upper bound.

lte.description: Lte is an inclusive upper bound.

elephant.distribution.RawVector.description: RawVector is an embedding supplied by the caller.

values.description: Values of the embedding, which must have the dimension of the index.

activate.description: Activate the new generation immediately. Defaults to false; callers typically register first and activate as a separate step so they can inspect the diff first.

description.description: Description is an optional human-readable tag for the new generation.

renditions.description: Renditions the generation should contain, one per asset kind. Order of the sources within each kind is preserved.

schemas.description: Schemas the generation should contain. Order is preserved.

types.description: Types the generation should contain. Order is preserved.

elephant.distribution.RematerializationS.description: RematerializationStatus is the state of one partition rebuild.

complete.description: Complete is true once the rebuild has finished and the old mounts have been dropped.

documents.description: Documents is how many documents have been written to the rebuild so far, and the size of the finished partition once it is done.

phase.description: Phase is the step the rebuild is at, and "done" when it has finished.

replaced.description: Replaced are the mounted archive indexes the rebuild takes over from.

revision.description: Revision is which generation of the partition the rebuild produces, counting the copy the original archival produced as zero.

started_at.description: StartedAt and UpdatedAt bound the run, RFC3339.

trigger.description: Trigger is what ordered the rebuild: "manual", "overlay", "erasure" or "rollup".

type.description: Type, Language and Period identify the partition.

language.description: Language segment of the partition, e.g. "sv". This is the index language series, not a document language attribute.

period.description: Period of the partition: "yyyyq[1-4]" for a quarter, or "yyyy" to roll a whole year of quarters into one partition.

type.description: Type of the partition to rebuild, e.g. "core/article".

elephant.distribution.RendererAttributes.description: RendererAttributes is the attribute names permitted on one element. A message rather than a repeated value because a proto3 map cannot carry a list directly.

elephant.distribution.RendererCircuitBre.description: RendererCircuitBreaker bounds the calls to a renderer and stops calling one that is failing. The breaker counts consecutive failures; every failure that reached the renderer counts against it, and one that never did - an unresolvable secret, or a call refused because the circuit is already open - does not.

failure_threshold.description: FailureThreshold is the number of consecutive failures that opens the circuit. Zero defaults to 5.

max_in_flight.description: MaxInFlight is the number of concurrent calls to the renderer. Zero defaults to 4. A call that cannot get a slot within the timeout is a failure, so the renderer contributes nothing to that document and its blocks fall back to the built-ins.

open_duration.description: OpenDuration is how long the circuit stays open before one half-open probe is let through, as a duration string. Empty defaults to 30 seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout of one renderer call, as a duration string ("1s", "750ms"). Empty defaults to one second. It bounds the whole call, waiting for an in-flight slot included, and it is the interrupt deadline of a "js" renderer too.

elephant.distribution.RendererConfigurat.description:
RendererConfiguration is one operator-registered HTML renderer: a script that runs in-process, or an HTTP endpoint that is called.
 A renderer failure of any kind - timeout, open circuit, connection error, non-2xx status, bad response signature, unreadable response, script exception, unresolvable secret - makes the renderer contribute nothing: every block renders exactly as if the renderer had returned no entry for it, by its built-in renderer where there is one, and delivery proceeds. HTML is an additive convenience; the absence of one custom block never stops a response or a push.

allow_insecure.description: AllowInsecure permits a plain http endpoint. For an in-cluster renderer reached over a trusted network; the HMAC authentication is unaffected either way, but the payload is then in the clear.

document_types.description: DocumentTypes narrows the renderer to the given document types. Empty is every type the generation renders HTML for.

kind.description:
Kind is "js" for a script run in-process, or "remote" for an HTTP endpoint.
 A string rather than an enum, as anchor and TypeDeliveryField.kind are: the zero value has to be invalid, so that a declaration that forgot its kind is refused rather than silently accepted as one of them.

name.description: Name identifies the renderer. It labels the metrics and the log lines, and it is the name of the renderer's secret, so it matches ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*$ - the pattern an environment variable name can be derived from.

policy_preset.description: PolicyPreset names a built-in sanitizer policy instead of spelling one out: "strict" or "rich-text". Mutually exclusive with policy.

revision.description: Revision is the cache-busting counter of the renderer's output, and it must be at least 1. The rendered HTML is cached on the identity of the configuration that produced it, and a remote renderer's own output is not part of that identity - so a deploy of the renderer that changes what it emits must bump this, or the cache keeps serving what the previous revision rendered. Output changes are configuration changes by contract.

script.description: Script is the renderer script, for the "js" kind. It is the script content, not a path: the operator tooling resolves its script_file before the call, exactly as it does for a type's transform script. Mutually exclusive with url.

triggers.description:
Triggers decide when this renderer is invoked: the document is in the renderer's document_types scope and one of its top-level content blocks matches one of the triggers. Zero triggers invoke the renderer for every rendered document of those types.
 A trigger is an invocation condition and nothing more. The request carries the whole document either way, and the renderer decides for itself which of its top-level blocks it answers for.

url.description:
URL is the endpoint to POST the render request to, for the "remote" kind. Mutually exclusive with script.
 It must be https unless allow_insecure is set. Unlike a push destination's endpoint it is not checked against a forbidden-address predicate: a renderer is configured by an operator on a "dist_admin" surface, and an in-cluster renderer on a private address is the expected deployment.

elephant.distribution.RendererPolicy.description: RendererPolicy is the sanitizer applied to a renderer's output. What it does not allow is removed; an entry whose HTML the policy reduces to nothing is a rendered-empty block, not a failure.

attributes.description: Attributes are the permitted attributes per element name, e.g. "a" -> ["href"]. An element with no entry keeps no attributes.

elements.description: Elements are the permitted element names, e.g. "p", "em", "aside".

url_schemes.description: URLSchemes are the permitted URL schemes on attributes that carry one, e.g. "https".

elephant.distribution.RendererSecretStat.description: RendererSecretStatus is what the API says about a stored renderer secret: that it exists, when it was written, and which keyring entry it is sealed under. Never its value.

key_id.description: KeyID names the keyring entry it is encrypted under. It is the input to a key rotation.

name.description: Name of the renderer the secret belongs to.

updated_at.description: UpdatedAt is when it was last written, RFC 3339.

elephant.distribution.RendererTrigger.description: RendererTrigger is one condition that invokes a renderer. It selects when the renderer is called, never what it is sent: the request carries the whole document, and the renderer is free to answer for any of its top-level blocks.

block_types.description: BlockTypes that invoke the renderer, e.g. "core/factbox", matched against the document's top-level content blocks. Empty is every block type.

roles.description: Roles narrows the trigger to blocks carrying one of the given roles. Empty is every role.

elephant.distribution.RenditionConfigura.description: RenditionConfiguration configures delivery-time rendition generation for one asset kind.

default_extension.description: DefaultExtension is the extension used when a request doesn't specify one.

default_variants.description: DefaultVariants are the variants generated when a request doesn't specify any.

kind.description: Kind is the asset kind, e.g. "image".

elephant.distribution.RenditionParameter.description: RenditionParameters selects the renditions to generate for one asset kind at delivery time.

extension.description: Extension of the generated renditions, e.g. "jpg". Empty falls back to the kind's configured default extension.

variants.description: Variants to generate rendition links for. Empty falls back to the kind's configured default variants.

elephant.distribution.RenditionSource.description: RenditionSource matches asset references in documents and maps them to an asset CDN namespace. Sources are evaluated in order; the first match wins.

block_types.description: BlockTypes are the document block types to inspect. Optional, defaults per kind ("core/image" for the "image" kind).

link_rel.description: LinkRel is the block link rel that carries the asset reference. Optional, defaults per kind ("image" for the "image" kind).

link_types.description: LinkTypes are the accepted types of the asset reference link.

name.description: Name identifies the source within its kind.

namespace.description: Namespace is the asset CDN namespace to build rendition URLs in.

uri_pattern.description: URIPattern is an anchored regular expression with exactly one capture group that extracts the asset ID from the link URI.

elephant.distribution.ResumeAction.description: ResumeAction is what happens to what accumulated in a destination's queue.

skip_to_event_id.description: SkipToEventId names the position by event id instead, which is what an operator reading a lag alert has to hand. It is resolved to a sequence, and the sequence used is reported back.

skip_to_seq.description: SkipToSeq is the queue position to skip to, inclusive. The queue is ordered by its own sequence rather than by event id, because an obligation-driven erasure row has no event, so a sequence is the only thing that can name every row.

skipped_seq.description: SkippedSeq is the sequence the skip was applied up to, and SkippedRows how many rows it stamped.

elephant.distribution.ResumeFrom.description: ResumeFrom is where delivery picks up again.

busy_subscriptions.description: BusySubscriptions are the ones that were not given a replay position because one was already running for them. They are resumed - the suspension is lifted - but the position they would have replayed from was not written, because there is one replay position per subscription and overwriting it would lose whichever came first with nothing to say it had. Rewind them individually once their current catch-up finishes.

resumed_from_event_id.description: ResumedFromEventId is the position the replay runs from, zero when resuming at the head.

still_stalled_destinations.description: StillStalledDestinations are destinations of the owner that are stopped because their queue passed a limit. A suspension and a stall are different things and lifting one does not lift the other, so these need ResumeDestination.

acknowledge_blind_window.description: AcknowledgeBlindWindow runs a replay that crosses the introduction of a delivery field the rules reference. Below that boundary the field is absent from every stored row, so a condition on it is a no-match rather than a missing input, and the replay under-delivers in a way nothing else would report.

from_event_id.description:
FromEventId is where the replay starts, exclusive. It may be below the position the subscription was created at - "start me from Monday" for a feed created on Tuesday is the case this call exists for - and the replay evaluates the rules over that window even though ordinary matching never looks below the creation position.
 Refused while a catch-up is already running for the subscription, or while it is waiting for its first evaluation, because there is one replay position per subscription and a second one would overwrite the first with nothing to say it had.

reason.description: Reason is recorded with the operation.

blind_before_event_id.description: BlindBeforeEventId is the boundary below which the replay evaluates rules against rows that predate a field they reference, when the caller acknowledged one. Zero when there is none.

from_event_id.description: FromEventId the replay will run from.

max_rows.description: MaxRows bounds one call, so that a rotation over a large deployment is a sequence of calls rather than one long transaction. Zero uses the server's own bound.

current_key_id.description: CurrentKeyId is the keyring entry rows were rotated to.

rotated.description: Rotated in this call, and remaining under an older key. A retired key is safe to remove from the environment when remaining is zero.

elephant.distribution.Rule.description: Rule is one node of the tree: a group of other rules, or a condition over one delivery field.

id.description: Id is stable across edits and is what provenance reports, so a match can say which condition admitted it. Assigned by the editor; the server stores and echoes it and derives nothing from it.

elephant.distribution.RuleSet.description: RuleSet is a delivery subscription's matching method: the tree the server evaluates, plus whatever the editor needs to draw it again.

editor_state.description:
EditorState is whatever the editor needs to reconstruct its own view - block coordinates, collapsed groups, comments. Stored and returned verbatim. The server never parses it, never validates it and never derives behaviour from it: the tree is what matches.
 Tree and editor state can therefore disagree if a client writes one without the other. That is the accepted cost of keeping the model in protobuf rather than in the editor's serialization format.

editor_version.description: EditorVersion lets a client detect a tree written by a newer editor, or by a caller that is not the editor at all, and fall back to a read-only rendering generated from the tree.

elephant.distribution.S3Credentials.description: S3Credentials are the keys a destination writes to its bucket with.

session_token.description: SessionToken is optional, for a temporary credential.

elephant.distribution.S3Transport.description: S3Transport is an S3 or S3-compatible bucket.

endpoint.description:
Endpoint overrides the S3 endpoint for an S3-compatible store. An endpoint override also turns on path-style addressing, which is what those stores expect.
 It must be an https URL, and it must not resolve to an address on the loopback, link-local, private or unique-local ranges. We sign requests with your credentials and write your documents to whatever this names, so a plaintext endpoint puts both on the wire in the clear, and an internal address points them at something that is not yours. The address is checked when the destination is written and again on every connection, so a name that changes what it resolves to later is refused then rather than followed.

prefix.description: Prefix every object key is written under, without a trailing slash. Empty writes at the root of the bucket, which is legal and is usually not what anybody wants.

region.description: Region of the bucket. Required, and not defaulted: an SDK that resolves a region from the ambient environment resolves the wrong one, and it does it at the first send rather than here.

elephant.distribution.SFTPCredentials.description: SFTPCredentials authenticate to the customer's SSH server. At least one of the two has to be set, and both may be - the key is offered first.

private_key.description:
PrivateKey is an unencrypted private key, in OpenSSH or PEM form.
 An encrypted key is refused rather than stored beside its passphrase: a passphrase would be a second secret to hold, rotate and lose, and it would sit in the same encrypted row as the key it protects. Decrypt it first: ssh-keygen -p -N '' -f <file>.

elephant.distribution.SFTPTransport.description:
SFTPTransport writes into a directory on a customer's SSH server.
 The username, the path and the host keys are here rather than in the credential because credentials are write-only at every scope: a username sealed with the secret could never be shown back, and a host key is public - pinning something nobody can read back is not verification.

host.description:
Host of the SSH server. A bare hostname or an IP address, without a scheme and without a port.
 It must not resolve to an address on the loopback, link-local, private, unique-local or carrier-grade-NAT ranges. A destination names somewhere of yours; those are somewhere of ours. The address is checked when the destination is written and again on every connection, so a name that changes what it resolves to later is refused then rather than followed.

host_keys.description:
HostKeys are the server's public keys in authorized_keys form - "ssh-ed25519 AAAA... [comment]". At least one is required, and a server presenting a key that is not one of these is refused.
 There is no trust-on-first-use and no accept-and-log mode. More than one key may be given so that a server can be rekeyed without an outage: add the new key, let the server rotate, remove the old one. Certificate host keys are not supported.

path.description: Path is the directory objects are written into. An absolute path is taken literally; a relative one is resolved against wherever the account lands, which on a chrooted account is its home. It is created if it is missing and we are allowed to, and a failure to create it is logged rather than fatal - an account that may write but not read cannot be checked, and refusing such an account would refuse a working destination.

port.description: Port of the SSH server. Defaults to 22.

public_key.description:
PublicKey is the authorized_keys line of the private key that was just stored, for the customer to install on their server. Empty for a credential that carries no key.
 It is on this response rather than on CredentialStatus because it is derived from the plaintext in hand. A readable projection of a write-only credential would need either a column of its own or a decryption on a read path reachable with dist_subscribe, which is the oracle credentials are write-only to avoid.

name.description: Name of the renderer the secret belongs to, matching RendererConfiguration.name. The renderer need not be configured yet.

secret.description: Secret is the shared secret the HMAC request and response signatures are computed with. It never crosses the wire to the renderer itself.

desired.description: Desired state of the sync worker, either "running" or "paused".

elephant.distribution.SigningKey.description: SigningKey is the public half of one transparency-log signing key: the JWK the JWKS endpoint publishes, with its fields broken out.

issued_at.description: IssuedAt is when the key was created, in the canonical fixed-width RFC 3339 form the events use ("2006-01-02T15:04:05.000000Z", UTC).

key_id.description: KeyID is what the second segment of a signature names.

not_before.description: NotBefore and NotAfter bound the window the key signs in. They are worth checking against an entry's created_at - a signature made outside its key's window verifies arithmetically but should not have existed - and they are why a key is published before it is used: a verifier needs it in hand before the first entry it signs arrives.

x.description: X is the base64url-encoded (unpadded) big-endian x coordinate of the public point, 48 bytes decoded. As in a JWK, so a client can hand {kty, crv, x, y} straight to a JWK importer.

y.description: Y is the y coordinate, same encoding.

elephant.distribution.SimilarityPercenti.description: SimilarityPercentile is one point of the similarity distribution.

percentile.description: Percentile the value is for, e.g. 50, 99 or 99.9.

similarity.description: Similarity at that percentile, on the same scale as VectorClauseMember.min_similarity.

reason.description: Reason is required. A cursor skip discards delivery decisions for every customer, and an unexplained one is indistinguishable afterwards from a bug.

to_event_id.description: ToEventId is where the cursor is moved to. Forward only: a target at or below the current cursor is refused, and so is one above the head of the log.

from_event_id.description: FromEventId is the cursor as it stood when the skip was recorded, and skipped_events how many events the move discards. The skip is applied by the matcher on its next pass, so this is what will happen rather than what has happened.

elephant.distribution.Sort.description: Sort sorts the hits on a field. Sort on keyword, date, boolean or numeric fields; text fields aren't sortable.

desc.description: Desc sorts in descending order instead of ascending.

elephant.distribution.StringValues.description: StringValues is the value of a flat index field. All field values are carried as strings regardless of the type of the field; dates are RFC 3339. A field is always a list because flattening a document collapses repeated blocks into parallel lists - values of the same block instance can't be paired up across fields.

values.description: Values of the field, in index order.

elephant.distribution.Subscription.description: Subscription is a stored subscription: its definition plus everything the server decided about it.

created_at.description: CreatedAt is when the subscription was created, RFC3339.

created_by.description: CreatedBy is the subject that created the subscription. Recorded for audit on organisation-owned subscriptions, where it does not confer ownership: any client of the organisation can manage and poll them.

deactivated_at.description: DeactivatedAt is when the subscription stopped matching because its keep-alive ran out, RFC3339. Empty while it is active, and on a durable subscription, which never lapses. A deactivated subscription no longer costs anything at match time and is removed altogether once its match log has expired.

enrolled_at_event_id.description:
EnrolledAtEventID is the eventlog position at which the matcher first evaluated this subscription. UNSET means it has not picked the subscription up yet, which is a state worth being able to see: it is the difference between "nothing has matched" and "nothing has looked yet". A subscription whose from_event_id is below the matcher's cursor is enrolled by replaying the events in between, so unset does not last longer than one pass unless the replay is still running.
 Optional rather than a plain int64 because zero is a real position: a subscription created against an empty log and enrolled on the matcher's first pass is enrolled at zero, and a presence-less field would report that as "not picked up yet" for ever. This mirrors the NULL the database column uses for the same distinction.
 Delivery subscriptions only.

error.description:
Error is set when the running server cannot evaluate the subscription - a rule tree it cannot parse, which is what a server rollback past the editor that wrote it looks like. The subscription is excluded from matching for as long as this is set, loudly rather than silently: an empty delivery that looks healthy is the failure this whole model is built to avoid. Empty when the subscription is fine.
 Delivery subscriptions only.

expires_at.description: ExpiresAt is when the subscription is deactivated unless it is touched before then, RFC3339. Empty on a durable subscription.

from_event_id.description: FromEventID is the distribution eventlog position the subscription starts at: the log head when it was created. Matching starts strictly above it, so a subscription never sees an event that was already in the log when it was registered. Assigned by the server - a client-chosen start position is a catch-up operation, not a creation parameter.

id.description: ID of the subscription, assigned by the server.

keep_alive_seconds.description: KeepAliveSeconds is the time the subscription survives untouched. Zero on a durable subscription, which does not expire. Independent of the ownership tier: either tier can be given a keep-alive, and either can be durable.

owner.description: Owner is the organisation of the creator for an organisation-owned subscription, and the subject of the creator for a session subscription.

owner_tier.description: OwnerTier is "org" for an organisation-owned subscription and "subject" for one owned by the subject that created it.

suspended_at.description:
SuspendedAt is when an administrator suspended the organisation's subscriptions, RFC3339. A suspended subscription matches nothing and its destinations are given nothing, including corrections to documents they already hold. Empty on an ordinary subscription.
 Delivery subscriptions only.

touched_at.description: TouchedAt is when the subscription was last touched, RFC3339. Empty on a durable subscription, which has no clock to reset.

updated_at.description: UpdatedAt is when the definition was last changed, RFC3339. Touches do not count as changes.

elephant.distribution.SubscriptionClass.description: SubscriptionClass is which matching method a subscription carries, and therefore which worker evaluates it and which storage holds it. It is derived from the spec, never stored: there is no column that can disagree with the branch.

elephant.distribution.SubscriptionMatch.description: SubscriptionMatch is one document event that matched a subscription. Matches are recorded once per (subscription, event) and delivery is at-least-once, so a client can see the same event twice after a restart; the event ID is what makes it safe to deduplicate.

event_id.description: EventID is the distribution eventlog ID of the event that matched. It is the cursor of the match log, and it is the same ID the event has in Content.GetNewDocuments.

event_time.description: EventTime is when distribution emitted the event, RFC3339. It is distribution's own clock, not the publication date: an event for historical content has an event_time of when it was ingested.

matched_at.description: MatchedAt is when the match was recorded, RFC3339. It normally trails event_time by seconds; a large gap means the match was made while catching up after an outage, and whether that is still worth alerting on is a decision for the client. Nothing is dropped for being late.

published_at.description: PublishedAt is when the version was published in the source system, RFC3339 - the publication date of the content, as opposed to event_time. It is the same value Content.GetNewDocuments reports as the event's published_at.

uuid.description: UUID of the document. Pass it to Content.GetDocument to fetch the document itself.

version.description: Version of the document that matched.

elephant.distribution.SubscriptionSpec.description: SubscriptionSpec is the definition of a subscription: everything about it that the client decides. Ownership, expiry and timestamps are not part of it, they are assigned by the server and read back on Subscription.

delivery_tags.description:
DeliveryTags are applied to the payload of every delivery this subscription admits, unioned over the subscriptions that admitted it. A property of the rule set rather than of the tree: customers route on them in their own ingest, and a delivery that no rule admitted - a correction to a document the destination has had before - carries none, because there is no rule to take them from.
 Delivery subscriptions only.

document_types.description: DocumentTypes to evaluate against. Required, at least one: a subscription always names the types it is about. A type that isn't indexed is an invalid argument.

language.description: Language to match, as the language tag documents are indexed under, e.g. "sv" or "sv-se". Empty matches every language. Unlike a search query, which is per language series (see Search.Query), leaving the language out costs nothing here: matching runs per incoming document, so there is no fan-out.

max_age_seconds.description: MaxAgeSeconds only matches documents first published within this many seconds of the event. Zero, the default, matches whatever the query and the clauses match, however old the document is. Set it on alert-style subscriptions: an update to a years-old article is a fresh event and would otherwise fire the alert.

notify_once.description: NotifyOnce suppresses re-notification for a document this subscription has already matched, whatever the later event on it is. Off by default, in which case a correction to a matched document is a new match with its own event type, which is usually what an editorial consumer wants. Composes with max_age_seconds rather than replacing it.

vector_clauses.description: VectorClauses are the semantic part of the subscription. All of them have to be satisfied, and they are ANDed with the query. An empty list means the subscription is the query alone.

expressions.description: Expressions to use to extract document contents.

owner_tier.description: OwnerTier and owner name whose delivery stops. Unlike everywhere else in this service the owner IS taken from the request: this is an administrative action taken about somebody else.

suspended_at_event_id.description: SuspendedAtEventId is the log head at suspension, recorded on every affected subscription so that a resume can replay from it.

elephant.distribution.TermQuery.description: TermQuery matches an exact, unanalysed value. Use it for keyword, boolean, date and numeric fields; a term query against a text field matches individual analysed tokens, which is rarely what you want.

boost.description: Boost multiplies the score contribution of the clause. Defaults to 1.

value.description: Value that the field must have.

elephant.distribution.TermsQuery.description: TermsQuery matches documents where the field has any of the values.

boost.description: Boost multiplies the score contribution of the clause. Defaults to 1.

values.description: Values, any one of which is a match.

elephant.distribution.TextCondition.description:
TextCondition matches a text delivery field. It is UNANALYZED: a substring or prefix test over the text that was extracted when the document was stored, with no tokenizer, no stemming and no stopword list anywhere near it, and it is that in every subscription that can hold one, because the tree is delivery-only.
 The mode is named CONTAINS rather than MATCH for exactly that reason: MATCH would invite the assumption that it means what OpenSearch's match means, which it cannot - there is no analyzer without an index. A subscription that wants analyzed semantics is a notification subscription and says so with a query.
 Comparison is case-insensitive under Unicode simple case folding, on NFC-normalised text, on both sides.

field.description: Field must be declared with kind "text".

value.description: Value to look for. Empty is an invalid argument.

elephant.distribution.TextMatchMode.description: TextMatchMode is how a TextCondition looks for its value in the field. Declared at file level rather than nested in the condition because the OpenAPI renderer only registers file-level enums, and a nested one fails the specification generation outright.

elephant.distribution.ThresholdEstimate.description: ThresholdEstimate is what one candidate threshold would have cost in volume over the calibration window.

matched_documents.description: MatchedDocuments is the number of documents in the window that reached it.

matches_per_day.description: MatchesPerDay is matched_documents spread over the window. It is a rate over past traffic, not a forecast, and it is per clause: a subscription that ANDs this clause with a query or another clause will see fewer.

id.description: ID of the subscription to touch. Required.

expires_at.description: ExpiresAt is when the subscription is deactivated unless it is touched again before then, RFC3339. Empty on organisation-owned subscriptions.

anchor.description: Anchor selects how documents of the type are partitioned across the search indexes. An empty value is a non-temporal type: one unpartitioned index per language that is never archived. "first_published" partitions by the time of the document's first distribution event, which is immutable, so a document never moves between partitions. "time_expressions" partitions by the dates time_expressions extracts from the document, with everything from the current quarter onwards sharing one index.

bounded_collection.description: Set to true if this is a collection of documents that are bounded (limited in size). Bounded collections can be fetched by type and language in one go.

delivery_fields.description:
DeliveryFields declare this type's contribution to the deployment's delivery-field vocabulary: the stable public names a delivery rule may name, and how each one is read out of a document of this type.
 A name is one field deployment-wide. Several types declare it, each with its own expression, because a section is not in the same place in an article and in a planning item - but the kind and the description must agree, or the name means two things and a rule written against one of them silently under-delivers against the other. Disagreement is refused at registration.
 They are extracted on the store path, per version, into a table of their own. There is no backfill: a field added to the registry today is present on versions stored from its activation onward and absent from everything before it, which is exactly right for the matcher at the head of the log and is a boundary anything replaying history has to resolve for itself.
 The registry is capped - field count, per-field value count, and a per-row byte budget the declarations are checked against - because the extracted values are held in memory for every version in a matcher page while every candidate rule tree is evaluated.

embeddings.description:
Embeddings enables semantic indexing of the document type: its documents are chunked and embedded, its indexes are created with a vector field, and it can be searched and subscribed to by vector. Independent of the anchor: a non-temporal type can be embedded, and a partitioned one can be left BM25-only.
 The vector field is set at index creation and cannot be added afterwards, so enabling this for a type that already has indexes takes a new index generation. Turning it off leaves the field in place, unwritten. It also needs a deployment with an embedding sidecar; without one the type is indexed BM25-only whatever this says.

facet_expressions.description:
FacetExpressions extract the values the daily views of Content.ListPublishedVersions and Content.ListPlannedVersions can narrow on. They are evaluated on the store path, per version, and the result is stored with the version - so a facet only narrows the versions that were written after it was configured, and adding one means backfilling what is already stored.
 Extraction is configuration rather than code because a facet is not in the same place in every type: a flash, an article and a planning item all reference their section differently.

label_expressions.description: LabelExpressions are used to extract labels from documents.

time_expressions.description: TimeExpressions are used for extracting time ranges from documents.

transform_script.description: TransformScript is the transformation script for this document type.

variants.description: Variants are the allowed variants for the document type.

elephant.distribution.TypeDeliveryField.description: TypeDeliveryField declares one delivery field and how to read it out of a document of this type.

description.description: Description is the human-readable text an editor shows beside the field name. Optional, and where several types declare the same name the non-empty ones must agree.

expression.description: Expression is a newsdoc value extraction expression, the same language facet and time expressions are written in.

kind.description:
Kind is one of "keyword", "number", "text" or "geo", and it decides which kind of condition may name the field: keyword for equality against a value set, number for ranges, text for substring and phrase matching, geo for a distance from a point.
 A string rather than an enum, as anchor is: the zero value has to be invalid, so that a declaration that forgot its kind is refused rather than silently accepted as a keyword.
 "geo" values are read as "latitude,longitude" in decimal degrees; "number" values are read as decimal numbers. A value that cannot be read as its kind is dropped from the stored row, not stored as text.

name.description: Name of the delivery field. This is the name a delivery rule uses, so it is a public identifier and outlives the projection: it must not be an index field name. Several types may declare the same name.

elephant.distribution.TypeFacetExpressio.description: TypeFacetExpression extracts one facet's values from a document.

expression.description: Expression is a newsdoc value extraction expression. It should yield document UUIDs rather than labels - a facet filter matches exactly, with no analysis or case folding, and the client resolves display names itself.

name.description:
Name of the facet the extracted values belong to. Several expressions can share a name, and their values are unioned.
 The vocabulary is deliberately small; "section" is the one facet the daily views are built for.

expression.description: Expression is a newsdoc value extraction expression.

layout.description: Layout is the time/date format to use when parsing. Optional, defaults to RFC3339 or ISO 8601 for values annotated as dates.

timezone.description: Timezone is the timezone the time should be parsed in. Optional, most timestamps should include timezone information, if they don't, parsing will fall back to the default timezone that the repository has been configured with.

id.description: ID of the subscription to update. Required.

keep_alive_seconds.description: KeepAliveSeconds sets a new keep-alive, clamped to at most seven days. Absent leaves the current one alone; zero removes it and makes the subscription durable. Applies to both ownership tiers. The ownership tier itself cannot be changed.

elephant.distribution.VectorClause.description: VectorClause is one semantic condition of a subscription. Its members are ORed: the clause is satisfied when any of them passes, or, when the clause is negated, when none of them does. Several conditions are several clauses, and they are ANDed - "close to A or B, but not about C" is two clauses, one with A and B as members and one negated clause with C.

members.description: Members of the clause, at least one. Each carries its own threshold, so an OR can be built out of sources that are not equally easy to be close to.

negate.description: Negate inverts the clause: it is satisfied when no member passes, i.e. when the document is close to none of them. Use PreviewSubscription before trusting a negated clause - what it excludes cannot be seen in what it returns.

elephant.distribution.VectorClauseMember.description:
VectorClauseMember is one vector to compare documents against, with the similarity at which it counts as a match. Exactly one source must be set.
 A member passes when the document has an embedding at or above min_similarity: the document is scored as the highest similarity across its chunk embeddings, so a long document matches on the part of it that is about the member.
 Prefer text and exemplars over a raw vector. Both are stored with the source and the embedding model they were derived under, which is what lets the server re-embed them and recalibrate their thresholds when the model is upgraded. A raw vector cannot be re-derived, and a member that holds one is paused and flagged for the owner instead.

min_similarity.description:
MinSimilarity is the cosine similarity at or above which this member passes, in [-1, 1], where higher means closer and 1 means identical direction. The embeddings are normalized, so this is the same dial as a maximum inner product distance, and it is the same number as Hit.score for a knn query and KnnQuery.min_similarity - which is how a threshold is found without guessing, see CalibrateVectorClause and Search.Query.
 Required: absent is an invalid argument. The field is optional so that a threshold of 0 - close to anything that isn't pointing away - is distinguishable from not stating one.
 Thresholds are model-dependent and are not portable between deployments or across an embedding model upgrade. Treat one as something to recalibrate, not as a constant.

model.description: Model is the identifier of the embedding model the stored vector of this member was derived under. Set by the server on read, ignored on write.

text.description: Text to be close to, embedded server-side with the current model. The normal choice: a phrase or a paragraph describing the subject matter of the subscription.

elephant.distribution.VectorCondition.description: VectorCondition is the semantic extension, and it is REFUSED at write time. Chunk vectors are produced by the indexer and stored in OpenSearch, so a delivery subscription that needed them would depend on the index - which is the one thing the two-class split exists to prevent. It is declared rather than omitted because this is where semantic delivery rules will go once embedding moves to the store path, and reserving the field number and the editor block now is free.

min_similarity.description: Required. Model-dependent, not portable, recalibrate rather than copy - see VectorClauseMember.min_similarity.

model.description: Model is set by the server on read.

newsdoc.Block.description: Block is the building block for data embedded in documents. It is used for both content, links and metadata. Blocks have can be nested, but that's nothing to strive for, keep it simple.

content.description: Content is used to embed content blocks.

contenttype.description: ContentType is used to describe the content type of the block/linked entity if it differs from the type of the block.

links.description: Links are used to link to other resources and documents.

meta.description: Meta is used to embed metadata

name.description: Name is a name for the block. An alternative to "rel" when relationship is a term that doesn't fit.

rel.description: Rel describes the relationship to the document/parent entity.

role.description: Role is used either as an alternative to rel, or for nuancing the relationship.

sensitivity.description: Sensitivity can be use to communicate how the information in a block can be handled. It could f.ex. be set to "internal", to show that it contains information that must be removed or transformed before publishing.

title.description: Title is the title/headline of the block, typically used in the presentation of the block.

type.description: Type is the type of the block

uri.description: URI is used to reference another entity in a document.

url.description: URL is a browseable URL for the the block.

uuid.description: UUID is used to reference another Document in a block.

value.description: Value is a value for the block. Useful when we want to store a primitive value.

content.description: Content is the content of the document, this is essentially what gets rendered on the page when you view a document.

language.description: Language is the language used in the document as an IETF language tag. F.ex. "en", "en-UK", "es", or "sv-SE".

links.description: Links are links to other resources and entities. This could be links to topics, categories and subjects for the document, or credited authors.

meta.description: Meta is the metadata for a document, this could be things like teasers, open graph data, newsvalues.

title.description: Title is the title of the document, can be used as the document name, or the headline when the document is displayed.

type.description: Type is the content type of the document.

uri.description: URI identifies the document (in a more human-readable way than the UUID).

url.description: URL is the browseable location of the document (if any).

uuid.description: UUID is a unique ID for the document, this can for example be a random v4 UUID, or a URI-derived v5 UUID.

post.description: GetArchivedDocument returns a fresh presigned URL for a specific archived document version. Used to resolve replay bodies and to re-mint a URL a consumer let expire.
ListArchiveChunks lists archived eventlog chunks in order, for full ordered replay of the history that precedes the hot log.

ListArchivedDocuments enumerates the latest archived version of every document offloaded to the archive, for a current-state snapshot. Pair it with a Content.GetNewDocuments tail from watermark_event_id to reconstruct full current state.
ActivateConfigGeneration switches the active configuration to the generation with the given ID.

ActivateIndexGeneration makes a generation the one that search, threshold calibration and subscription matching read. The switch is atomic and exactly one generation is active at a time.
 Activation is refused when the candidate lags the head of the eventlog by more than a small gate, ten events by default, because a generation that is behind would answer with stale content the moment it took over. It is refused on the same gate when the candidate stands that far above the position the outgoing generation has matched up to, since that distance is what the matching handover has to replay and an outgoing generation that is stalled or disabled can be arbitrarily far behind a candidate that is on the head. Force activates regardless, which is the right call when the outgoing generation is unreachable and the wrong one otherwise.
 Subscription matching is handed over rather than dropped. Activation records the position the outgoing generation had matched up to and stops its matching there; the incoming generation replays the events from that position up to its own cursor for matching only. Match rows are keyed on subscription and event, so replaying an event is idempotent - but the two generations read the log in different pages, and a document that occurs more than once in a page is matched under the last event of that page, so the same document version can end up recorded under two events. Delivery across a cutover is at-least-once with the occasional duplicate: deduplicate on the subscription, the document UUID and the version if that matters to you.

CreateIndexGeneration registers a new index generation: a complete set of search indexes with an index name prefix of its own, built on one of the OpenSearch clusters the deployment declares.
 The generation is populated by the ordinary backfill - the indexer that picks it up drains the archive and then tails the eventlog - while the active generation keeps serving. Subscription matching is suppressed for the whole build, so creating a generation never re-notifies a subscription, but the percolator indexes are seeded as it goes, so matching works from the moment it is activated.
 Use it to rebuild the index from scratch after a mapping change that cannot be applied to live indexes, or to move the index to another cluster - which is how an OpenSearch major version upgrade is done: create a generation on the new cluster, watch it catch up with ListIndexGenerations, compare results through the generation override on Search.Query, activate, and delete the old one.

DeleteIndexGeneration deletes an inactive generation. The active generation cannot be deleted - activate another one first.
 The call records the deletion and returns; the cleanup runs asynchronously and is scoped by the generation's index prefix: its document, percolator and overlay indexes, the bookkeeping rows that name them, its eventlog cursor, and the snapshots under the generation's base path in the snapshot repository. Nothing outside the prefix is touched, so deleting a generation can never take content away from the one that is serving.

DeleteRendererSecret removes a stored renderer secret. It does not invalidate a configuration generation that names the renderer: the renderer is skipped at render time, its blocks fall back to the built-in renderers, and the missing-secret gauge is raised.

EraseDocument erases a document's content from every store we control: the hot version rows, the archived objects, the search index copies, the extracted delivery fields and the cached fragments. It never touches the eventlog, whose entries carry identifiers and hashes only, so the transparency log survives an erasure with its hash chain intact.
 Erasure is point-in-time. It removes the content that exists when it is ordered and does not blocklist the UUID: a document re-published afterwards is a new document and is distributed and indexed normally.
 It also STOPS THE CONTENT GOING OUT and tells everybody who was given it. Undelivered queue rows for the document are dropped, and every destination that was ever pushed a copy is sent a deletion marker in the same feed the content arrived in - the ordinary marker envelope, at the next entry of that document's chain, saying "deleted". Nothing is deleted at a destination: push is append-only, we do not control what a customer retains, and a marker is the only honest instrument we have.
 THIS CALL IS NOT THE ORDINARY TRIGGER. Deleting a document in the repository erases it here: the delete event drives the same erasure this RPC records, and an editorial delete inside becomes an erasure outside. What the RPC is for is the content that trigger cannot reach - a document deleted before distribution ingested delete events, and content that exists here only as imported history with no live repository document to delete. Calling it for a document that has already been erased is a no-op and safe.
 The call is idempotent and returns the recorded request. A request is complete once no archived index snapshot holds a copy any more, which can require the affected partitions to be re-materialized, and once every destination that was given a copy has been told - the marker delivered, or the destination and its credentials gone. Use GetErasureStatus to prove completion.
 What it has never covered, and cannot: content a customer has already ingested from a destination into their own systems. We do not delete files on a customer's machine and do not claim to.
GetActiveConfigGeneration returns the currently active generation, including its schemas and type configurations. Supports long polling for changes.
GetAllActiveSchemas returns the schemas in the active generation. Supports long polling so clients can watch for changes.
GetDocumentTypes lists the document types declared by schemas in the active generation.

GetErasureStatus returns the recorded erasure request for a document and what it is still waiting for: the archived index partitions awaiting re-materialization, and the delivery destinations that were given a copy and have not been told.
 One narrow window sits outside the proof, and it is stated here rather than left to a design document. An object whose write completed but whose inventory row was never recorded - a process that died between the two, or a lost acknowledgement from the recipient - is indistinguishable from a file the customer put there themselves, so if it is the only copy a destination ever received, that destination is not on the list. The queue row survives, so the next pass re-sends and records it; the exposure is one restart intersected with an erasure.
GetSchema retrieves a stored schema spec by name and version.
GetSyncStatus returns the desired and current state of the distribution sync worker together with its position in the repository eventlog.
GetTypeConfiguration returns the configuration for a type in the active generation.
ListConfigGenerations lists historical generations, most recent first.

ListIndexGenerations lists the index generations together with the position each one's indexer has reached in the distribution eventlog and the current head of that log. That is the catch-up view a rebuild is followed through: a candidate is ready to be activated once its lag has come down to a handful of events.
ListRendererSecrets lists the stored renderer secrets by name, with the keyring entry each one is sealed under and when it was last written. Never their values.

RegisterConfigGeneration registers a complete configuration set (schemas + type configurations) as a new generation. Existing schema versions can be re-used by name and version without re-supplying the spec; if the spec is supplied for an existing version it must match the stored one. Returns the new generation ID.

RematerializePartition orders an archived index partition to be rebuilt from the archive: overlay corrections are folded in, deleted and erased documents are left out, and the result is built with the current mappings and schemas.
 The call records the order and returns; the rebuild itself runs in the index tiering job, which owns the snapshot repository and the warm tier. Call it again to see how far it has got - the response is the recorded state either way, and ordering a rebuild that is already under way changes nothing.
 A period of the form "yyyy" orders the rollup of a whole year: the years quarter partitions are rebuilt into a single yearly one and their mounts are dropped.

SetRendererSecret stores the shared secret a remote HTML renderer authenticates with. A renderer names its secret implicitly: the renderer "factbox-special" uses the secret "factbox-special".
 The secret is write-only. It is stored encrypted under the delivery keyring and there is no call that returns it; ListRendererSecrets reports which secrets exist and when they were written, and nothing else. An environment-provided secret takes precedence over a stored one, so an emergency override does not need a write here.
 Store the secret before registering a generation that names the renderer: registration resolves every remote renderer's secret and refuses a generation whose secrets are not resolvable.

SetSyncState sets the desired state of the distribution sync worker. A cold-started service (no configuration, no sync position) starts out paused so that the repository eventlog isn't consumed - and discarded - before a configuration generation has been activated.

CancelImport cancels an import. Cancellation is terminal: the job stops being claimable by the loader, the imports queued behind it proceed, and its hold on index maintenance is released. An un-finalized upload can be cancelled too, which retires its upload ID.
 Only a job that is not actively loading can be cancelled: a load that keeps failing backs off between passes with status "failed", which is when a cancel lands. Documents the job already published are signed log entries and stay published - remediation of loaded content is per-document erasure, not cancellation.
 Requires dist_admin.

CreateImportUpload starts a bulk import upload: the client declares the files that make up the import set and gets a presigned PUT URL back for each of them. The files are uploaded directly to object storage; the service only brokers the URLs. Files are gzipped NDJSON with one import envelope per line, and they are loaded in the order they were declared, so declare them in chronological (quarterly) order.
 To resume an upload that was cut short, call CreateImportUpload again with the upload ID and the same file declaration: fresh URLs are returned for every file, and only the ones that are missing or were interrupted need to be PUT again. Re-uploading a completed file is harmless - finalization verifies sizes and hashes, not upload counts. An upload that is never finalized is eventually cleaned up.
 Requires dist_admin, unlike the service's dist_read baseline, and fails with FailedPrecondition when the deployment has no archive bucket configured - there is nowhere to upload to.

FinalizeImportUpload declares an upload complete and turns it into an import job. The service verifies that every declared file is present in the bucket with the declared size and sha256 - a missing or mismatching file is a FailedPrecondition, and the upload stays open so the file can be re-uploaded and finalization retried - records the import, and starts loading asynchronously. The returned import ID is what GetImportStatus takes; the upload ID is consumed and invalid afterwards.
 Loaded documents go through the same store path as live content: document versions are upserted and the events enter the transparency log hashed and signed like any others, carrying the import's source so that consumers can tell bulk-imported content from the live repository flow. The load is resumable and idempotent per document version - a service restart continues where it left off.
 Requires dist_admin and an archive bucket, as CreateImportUpload.

GetDocument returns a single document, transparently falling back to the archive if the requested version (or the whole document) has been evicted from the hot data set. The document is returned in-band.

GetDocumentVersions loads a batch of document versions. It is the batch form of GetDocument, and it is how a client streams in the documents a listing left deferred.
 Responses that carry documents bound how many they carry, because a document whose body has aged out of the hot store is an archive read each and loading a whole page of them would make the response time a function of how far back the caller browsed. Entries beyond that bound come back with deferred set and no document; pass their UUID and version here to fetch them, in whatever order and at whatever rate suits the client - typically what is on screen first, and the rest as the reader scrolls.
 The same bound applies here: ask for more than the server will load in one response and the surplus comes back deferred again, so a client that keeps requesting what it did not get makes progress rather than looping.

GetImportStatus returns the recorded state of an import job: where the load has got to, and what went wrong if it failed.
 Requires dist_admin.

GetSigningKeys returns the public keys the transparency log's signatures are made with, so that a consumer reading the log with GetNewDocumentsRequest.verification can verify it without leaving the API it is already talking to.
 The same keys are served as a JWKS at the unauthenticated GET /signing-keys and mirrored into the archive bucket. Those remain the way an independent verifier with no credentials, checking archived content, gets them. This is the convenience for a consumer that already holds a client.
 An independent copy is worth keeping either way: keys fetched from the service that signed the log only prove it is internally consistent.

ListImports lists import jobs, most recent first.
 Requires dist_admin.

ListPlannedVersions lists what is planned for an interval, earliest first: the current version of every document of the requested types whose resolved anchor date falls in it.
 Only current versions, deliberately. A planning item's revisions are working state rather than publications, and a calendar showing five revisions of one item is noise - so unlike ListPublishedVersions this never carries version history. An item rescheduled out of the interval leaves it entirely rather than staying behind under its old date.
 Intended for forward-anchored types: planning items and calendar entries.

ListPublishedVersions lists the publication events of an interval, newest first: what was published, in the order it happened. Every stored version of every document of the requested types whose publication time falls in the interval, superseded ones included and marked as such, so that a correction sits at the minute it was made rather than under the document's latest version.
 This is the same log GetNewDocuments serves, read by publication time instead of by event ID. It is a range scan over the stored versions, not a search: the inputs are document types, an interval and facet values, the order is chronological, and there is no relevance, free-text or cross-type ranking to be had.
 Any interval can be listed, however old: retention drops document bodies and keeps the bookkeeping the listing is made of. Past inline_horizon the entries come back deferred and their documents are streamed in with GetDocumentVersions.
 Intended for backward-anchored types - articles, flashes, editorial information - where the question is what was published when. See ListPlannedVersions for the calendar view of forward-anchored types.

AttachSubscription attaches a delivery subscription to a destination. Both must have the same owner. The attachment records the log position it was made at, and everything above that position that the subscription matches is delivered - including the events between the attachment and the matcher noticing it, which are replayed.

CreateDestination registers a destination. It is created disabled unless the request says otherwise, because a destination with no credentials and no attached subscription is a destination being configured rather than one that is broken.

DeleteDestination marks a destination deleted and wipes its credentials. It is not a row deletion: the inventory of what the destination was given outlives it, because that is the record an erasure request is answered from, and there is no way left to tell the destination anything once the credentials are gone.
 For the same reason the deletion discharges the destination's outstanding erasure obligations, recorded as "destination_deleted". The inventory rows are kept as the record of what it was given.

DetachSubscription removes an attachment. Queue rows already written for the destination are still delivered: they are the destination's, not the subscription's, which is also why a document the destination has had keeps getting its corrections until the sticky window runs out.

GetCatchupStatus reports how a subscription's running catch-up is going: where it started, where it has got to, and - when the caller acknowledged a blind window - the boundary they accepted and how many events have actually been evaluated below it.
 The last number is why this call exists. Acknowledging a blind window accepts a shortfall, and without a reader for it the acknowledgement would be a one-way switch: accepted, and never measured.
GetDestination returns a destination as stored, with the status of its credentials but never their values.

ListDeliveryOperations lists the deliberate operator decisions not to deliver something: suspensions, resumes, destination skips, cursor skips and rewinds. It is the answer to "why is there a hole in this customer's feed", which is otherwise only in an incident note.
ListDestinations lists the destinations the caller can see: the ones owned by the organisation of the caller, and the ones owned by the calling subject.

ResumeDestination restarts a destination whose queue grew past its depth or age limit and stopped. The operator chooses what happens to what accumulated: deliver it, or skip up to a position. A skip stamps the rows skipped rather than deleting them, so what was not sent stays a query.
 Only a stalled destination can be resumed. On a running one a skip would stamp rows the worker is in the middle of sending, so a resume of a destination that is not stalled is refused with its state named.
 A resume also rebaselines the queue limits at the current end of the queue. Without that a drain cannot drain: the limit is checked before the first send of a pass, so a destination that stopped because its queue was too deep is still too deep the moment it restarts, and would stop again without delivering anything. What accumulated is delivered; the limits apply to what accumulates after.

ResumeSubscriptions lifts a suspension, from the position it was suspended at or from the head of the log. Resuming at the head leaves a gap, which is recorded rather than silent; resuming at the prior position replays the window, subject to the same two refusals RewindSubscription is subject to.

RewindSubscription replays a subscription from an earlier log position - "start me from Monday". It does not move the position the subscription started at, which stays as the record of where the feed began; it schedules a catch-up from the position given, which the matcher runs paged and resumably alongside its ordinary work.
 Refused below the retention horizon, naming it: below that the events and the extracted fields a rule would be evaluated against are both gone, so there is nothing to replay. Refused across the introduction of a field the rules reference, naming the boundary, unless acknowledge_blind_window is set - below that boundary the field is absent from every row and the rule reads as a no-match rather than as a missing input.

RotateDeliveryKeys re-encrypts stored credentials under the current keyring entry and reports how many rows still name an older one. A retired key is safe to remove from the environment when that number reaches zero.
SetDestinationCredentials writes one kind of credential for a destination, replacing whatever was there. There is no call that reads them back.

SkipDeliveryMatcher moves the delivery matcher's cursor forward, deliberately, leaving a recorded gap in every delivery feed.
 It exists for one situation: the matcher has fallen below the retention horizon, where the events it would read and the fields it would evaluate have both been deleted, and it has halted rather than deciding anything. The cursor cannot be moved by resuming a destination - a destination resume stamps rows in one queue, and the cursor is one row for the whole deployment - so this is its own call, and it records who moved it, from where, to where, and why.
 Forward only. The skip is a request the matcher applies at the top of its next pass; until then it is pending, which is visible.

SuspendSubscriptions stops delivery for an owner: every delivery subscription they own or one of their subjects created stops matching, and every destination they own stops sending. Rows already queued hold rather than drain, so a resume can still deliver them.
 It is not expiry and it is not credential revocation. A suspended owner's tokens carry whatever scopes the identity provider grants them, and cutting those is done there.

UpdateDestination replaces the definition of a destination. The spec is written whole: fields left out of it are cleared, not kept. Credentials are not part of the spec and are not touched. Changing the transport, format or name template restarts the destination's worker, so an in-flight send completes and the next one uses the new definition.

GetMappings returns the searchable fields of a document type and the type of each field, as the union across the language indexes. Use it to find out what can be queried, and how, before building a query.
Query searches one language series of one tier. Language is required and a query never fans out across languages: searching several languages is several calls.

CalibrateVectorClause is how a min_similarity gets chosen. It scores the given clause members against the documents of a recent window and returns the similarity distribution, the top hits to eyeball, and - the number the decision is actually made on - the estimated matches per day at a ladder of candidate thresholds. "At 0.62 this clause alone would have matched about 14 documents a day last week" is what a threshold means in practice; a suggested threshold is a volume target, never a claim about relevance.

CreateSubscription registers a new subscription and returns it as stored, with the ownership and expiry the server assigned to it. Matching starts at the next indexed document; documents that were indexed before the call are never matched, use PreviewSubscription to see what the subscription would have caught.

DeleteSubscription removes a subscription and its match log. Deleting is permanent and distinct from a subscription expiring: polling a deleted subscription is a not-found, polling an expired one is a failed precondition.

GetDeliveryFields returns the delivery-field vocabulary of the active configuration generation: the names a rule may reference, what kind of condition each admits, and which document types declare it.
 The last of those is what an editor needs to warn with. A condition on a field only some of a subscription's document types declare is a no-match on the rest, silently, because an absent key is a no-match by definition - so a rule over {article, planning-item} naming a field only articles declare delivers half of what it looks like it delivers.
 The registry is read from Postgres and needs no index. Listing does not count as a touch on anything.
GetSubscription returns a subscription as stored. Counts as a touch.

ListSubscriptions lists the subscriptions the caller can see: the ones owned by the organisation of the caller, and the ones owned by the calling subject. Listing does not count as a touch, so it is safe to poll for housekeeping without keeping abandoned subscriptions alive.

PollMatches reads the match log of a subscription, long-polling for new matches. Delivery is at-least-once and ordered by event ID, which doubles as the cursor: pass the highest event ID you have processed as after_event_id on the next call.
 Polling a subscription that has expired is a failed precondition, not a not-found: the subscription was abandoned rather than deleted, and the client can tell the two apart and re-create if it wants to. Counts as a touch, so a client that keeps polling never expires.

PreviewSubscription is the dry run of a complete subscription definition against a recent window: what would have matched, with the same provenance the match log carries. It is the acceptance test for a new subscription, and the only practical way to reason about a negated clause, which is invisible in the results it does not exclude.

TouchSubscription resets the keep-alive clock of a subscription without reading anything else. Ordinary use does not need it - PollMatches, GetSubscription and UpdateSubscription all count as touches - it is for clients that hold a subscription open while they are not polling. Touching a durable subscription is a no-op, it has no clock to reset.

UpdateSubscription replaces the definition of a subscription. The spec is written whole: fields left out of it are cleared, not kept. Vector clause members are re-embedded and the query part is re-translated, so an update takes effect for documents indexed after it returns. Counts as a touch.

tags.description:
Delivery is where a delivery subscription is wired to somewhere to deliver to. A subscription says what; a destination says where and how - transport, credentials and format - and the two are separate so that one drop can be fed by several differently-tuned subscriptions, and so that a subscription can be authored before anything is wired to a transport.
 Ownership is checked when a subscription is attached and re-checked every time the matcher writes a queue row: a subscription may only be attached to a destination with the same owner. The owner is never taken from the request - it is the organisation claim or the subject of the credentials - and owner_tier picks which of the two, defaulting to the organisation, exactly as it does on Subscriptions.
 Credentials are write-only. They are stored encrypted and there is no call that returns them; a destination reports which kinds it holds and when they were last written, and nothing else. Losing them is a re-entry, not a recovery.
 Access requires the "dist_subscribe" scope, which is granted by "dist_admin". The operator calls - SuspendSubscriptions, ResumeSubscriptions, ResumeDestination, SkipDeliveryMatcher, RotateDeliveryKeys and ListDeliveryOperations - require "dist_admin" on its own: they decide that content will not be delivered, and that is not a customer's decision to make about their own feed.
 v0.0.15 removed ClearDeliveryErasureObligation, the per-document erasure write-off. Erasure informs rather than withdraws: nothing is deleted at a destination, an unreachable destination's obligation is an ordinary undelivered queue row that delivers when the destination recovers, and DeleteDestination is the one write-off left - it removes the ability to deliver rather than recording that we will not.

tags.description: Archive exposes the offloaded eventlog history and document versions for bulk export - e.g. building or rebuilding a search index over the full content set. Bodies are delivered as presigned URLs that the consumer fetches directly from object storage; the service only brokers the catalog and mints the URLs. Object keys and the presigning mechanism are internal: consumers address content by identity (uuid, version, chunk_id), never by storage key.
tags.name: Archive

tags.description:
Search exposes the distribution search index: a query surface over the documents that Content delivers, with the same visibility rules. It is read-only.
 Access requires the "dist_search" scope, which is granted by "dist_read" (search is a view of what the caller can already fetch) and by "dist_admin".
tags.name: Search

tags.description:
Subscriptions are standing queries. Instead of polling Search for whatever is new, a client registers what it is interested in once, and the indexer evaluates every document it indexes against the registration. Matches land in a per-subscription log that the client reads with PollMatches; matching latency is indexing latency, a few seconds behind publication.
 A document matches when the query part matches, if there is one, and every vector clause is satisfied. Clauses are ANDed, the members of a clause are ORed, and a negated clause is satisfied when none of its members pass. OR across a text query and a vector clause is deliberately not expressible - that is two subscriptions.
 Ownership and expiry are two separate choices. The owner is never taken from the request - it is the organisation claim or the subject of the credentials the call was made with - and owner_tier picks which of the two, defaulting to the organisation. A keep-alive, independently of that, makes the subscription expire when it goes untouched for that long; without one it lives until it is deleted. See CreateSubscriptionRequest.
 Access requires the "dist_subscribe" scope, which is granted by "dist_admin".
